operations.description:
Retrieve a single product with its full marketplace detail.

This endpoint returns the live product record used across search, category browsing, and the product detail page. A product is the marketplace's core sellable item and belongs to one seller and one optional category. The response is intended to support customer viewing of the product name, description, base price, images, available variants, and review-related context.

The product may be associated with a category, including a subcategory, and may include multiple ordered images and purchasable variants. If the product has no variants, it remains visible for browsing but is not purchasable. If the product or its owning seller is no longer available for browsing according to platform rules, the request should fail with a not-found or unavailable-style response consistent with the service's standard error handling.

This operation is read-only and does not modify product state. Administrators may also use it as part of product oversight workflows, while sellers can use it to inspect their own listings.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the product by UUID primary key from mall_platform_products, joining the owning seller account, optional category, ordered images, and variants needed for the detail view. Include the complete live product row and its direct relations; do not return snapshot tables here because this endpoint is for the current product state, not historical reconstruction.

Use the product id from the path to fetch exactly one record. If the product does not exist or is unavailable under business rules, return a not-found response. The implementation should respect platform visibility rules for deleted products and unavailable seller states when determining whether the caller may see the item. Do not require a request body. Ensure related collections are returned in deterministic order, especially product images by sort_order and variants by creation or stable display order.

responseBody.description: The full product detail record including seller, category, images, variants, and review-related presentation data.

parameters.description: The product identifier in UUID format.
parameters.name: productId

operations.description:
Create a new sellable product for the authenticated seller.

A product is the marketplace’s core listing unit and is used in search results, category browsing, and product detail pages. Each product belongs to the seller who creates it and must be assigned to an existing category, including a subcategory when applicable. The product is created with its base commercial identity so it can later be extended with variants, images, and inventory.

The request must include the product name, description, category, and base price. The server must validate that the caller is an approved seller and that the category exists. If the seller is not allowed to sell, the request must be rejected. If validation fails or the category is invalid, the product must not be created.

On success, the newly created product is returned for immediate use in seller management screens. This operation does not create snapshots by itself; snapshots are created when the product is later edited.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert a new row into mall_platform_products for the authenticated seller.

Resolve the seller identity from the authenticated session and reject the request if the account is unavailable for selling, not approved, suspended, banned, or otherwise not permitted to create products. Validate that the referenced category exists and is an allowed category/subcategory target for product assignment. Persist the product with the required business fields only; do not invent or infer any missing fields beyond the actual schema.

Use a transaction if any downstream checks or related writes are needed. If the create fails, return a validation or business error and ensure no partial product record remains. The created product should be immediately retrievable through detail and listing endpoints. Snapshot creation is not part of this operation; it is handled by product update workflows.

responseBody.description: The newly created product with its persisted fields.

requestBody.description: Product creation data for the authenticated seller.

operations.description:
Update a seller-owned product.

This operation lets the owning seller revise the product's live marketplace data, including its name, description, category, and base price. The product is the root catalog record for a sellable item, while images, variants, and historical snapshots are managed in related tables. A successful update must preserve the marketplace history by creating a product snapshot that captures the prior state before the edit is applied.

The updated product remains tied to the same seller account and category structure. If the referenced category is removed or the product is otherwise unavailable, the request must be rejected according to the platform's business rules. If the seller does not own the product, the operation must fail with an authorization error. Any snapshot created by this operation must include the preserved product data and related presentation state needed for later audit or dispute review.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the product by id and verify it exists and is not deleted for the purpose of editing. Confirm the current authenticated seller owns the product; administrators may be allowed only if the broader authorization layer grants product oversight rights. Validate the incoming product fields against the actual product schema: name, description, category_id, and base_price are the editable live fields exposed by the table. Do not accept or persist seller_account_id changes through this endpoint.

Before applying the update, create a product snapshot row capturing the product's previous state, including the current name, description, category label if available, base price, main image URI, and the current counts of images and variants. Because product snapshots have related image and variant snapshot tables, the service should also persist the snapshot composition needed by downstream snapshot readers. The live update should then modify only the product row itself in a transaction.

If category_id is provided, ensure it references an existing category and that the category is allowed by business rules, including subcategory selection if applicable. Reject invalid categories, missing products, or ownership violations. If the product has been deleted or is otherwise unavailable for editing, return a not-found or conflict-style business error consistent with the project conventions. On any failure after snapshot preparation, roll back all database changes so the product and its snapshot history remain consistent.

responseBody.description: Updated product details after the seller's changes have been applied.

parameters.description: Identifier of the product to update.
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: Fields to update on the product.

operations.description:
Permanently removes a product from the active marketplace catalog.

This operation deletes the targeted product when the caller is authorized and the product satisfies all deletion restrictions. A product may only be removed when none of its variants have pending paid or shipped order items, and when none of its variants have pending cancellation requests or refund requests. When deletion is allowed, the product is removed from active browsing, its variants are removed from active use, and the related inventory records are removed from active use as well.

Historical records remain available for dispute review and audit purposes through the platform's snapshot data. Deleted products must no longer appear in search results or category listings, and administrators may invoke this operation for policy enforcement across the platform. The service must reject deletion attempts that violate pending order, cancellation, or refund constraints.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the product by productId and verify it exists. Enforce authorization so that only the owning seller or an administrator can perform the deletion.

Before deleting, check all product variants for blocking conditions: any order items in paid or shipped status, any pending cancellation requests, and any pending refund requests. If any blocking record exists, return a validation error and do not modify the database.

When deletion is allowed, delete the product and cascade deletion of its variants and their active inventory records within a single transaction. Remove the product from active catalog visibility so it no longer appears in search or category browsing. Do not delete historical snapshot records; preserve them for seller or administrator review. If wishlist or other references depend on the product being active, ensure the active catalog state marks it unavailable rather than exposing broken references.

Use transactional safeguards to prevent partial deletion. If any step fails, roll back the entire operation. Return a not-found error when the product does not exist, a forbidden error when the caller lacks permission, and a conflict or validation error when deletion restrictions are not satisfied.

parameters.description: Identifier of the product to permanently remove from the active catalog.
parameters.name: productId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of variants that belong to a specific product.

This operation is used to browse the purchasable options for one product within its product context. Each variant represents a concrete SKU-level choice such as a color or size combination, and the returned summaries should reflect the variant's SKU code, option values, pricing override, and current availability state derived from inventory.

The product scope is fixed by the path parameter. The request body is used only for list controls such as pagination, keyword matching, sorting, and filters. Products with no variants must still be handled gracefully by returning an empty page rather than an error, and globally unique SKU rules must be enforced when variant data is displayed or edited through related operations.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_product_variants for the given product ID with pagination and optional filtering. Join to mall_platform_inventory_records only if the response summary requires stock-derived availability; otherwise compute availability via the service layer from the variant's current inventory position. Filter strictly by mall_platform_product_id equal to the path productId. Support search across sku_code and option_values if the request schema includes a keyword field. Sort by the requested sort key, defaulting to newest-first or by creation time when unspecified.

Return a paginated summary list. Do not include variants from other products. If the product does not exist, return a not-found error. If the caller lacks access to the owning seller's product, enforce authorization before querying. Do not duplicate productId in the request body. Ensure inactive or out-of-stock variants are still listed if the business rules require visibility, but surface their current status accurately. The response type must be paginated because this is an index operation.

operations.description:
Retrieve the stock movement history for a specific product variant.

Inventory records represent the append-only accounting trail of quantity changes for one variant, including restocking, stock adjustments, and order-related movement. This operation lets sellers inspect how the current stock position was derived over time and review the recorded reason and timestamp for each change.

The inventory history is always scoped to the specified product variant. Consumers must treat the path parameter as the owning variant context and should not attempt to query records across variants through this endpoint. The returned list is intended for operational review and dispute investigation, so it should preserve chronological accuracy and support paging for variants with long histories.

If the variant does not exist, or the caller is not allowed to access the variant’s inventory history, the service should reject the request using the platform’s standard not-found or forbidden handling. Empty history is a valid result for a newly created variant with no stock movement yet.

Order results by the requested sort column, defaulting to newest inventory record first, and paginate the result set using limit/offset or cursor-based paging consistent with the project’s list patterns.
Return a paginated summary response containing each inventory record’s identifier, quantity change, reason, and timestamp.

operations.description:
Retrieve and update the authenticated customer's shopping cart in one request.

This operation allows a customer to review the current cart state and apply cart-level changes such as quantity adjustments before checkout. The cart is owned by a single customer account, and each cart line represents one selected product variant, so all changes are applied only within the authenticated customer's scope.

The service must verify that referenced variants are still valid and that the cart remains internally consistent after the update. If a requested change cannot be completed, the cart must remain unchanged and the caller should receive a validation error. When the update succeeds, the service recalculates line subtotals and the cart total from the persisted cart items.

Use the customer identity from the security context and do not accept ownership identifiers from the body.

Apply requested line changes against the existing cart items, ensuring each line continues to reference exactly one product variant.
Recalculate each item's subtotal and the cart total after changes are applied.
Validate referenced variants, quantity values, and cart ownership; if any validation fails, abort the transaction and return an error without modifying saved cart data.

operations.description:
Create the authenticated customer's shopping cart.

This operation initializes the customer-owned cart workspace used before checkout. A shopping cart groups selected product variants, tracks pre-order intent, and serves as the container for cart items that are later reviewed at checkout. If the customer already has an active cart, the service should return that cart rather than creating a duplicate container.

The cart is associated with one customer account and is intended for temporary purchase preparation only. Its contents are managed separately through cart item operations, which add, update, and remove specific variant lines. Validation should ensure the caller is an authenticated customer account and reject requests from unavailable account states.

Resolve the current authenticated customer account from the session context. If the account is not authenticated or is in an unavailable state, reject the request.

Do not create cart items in this operation. Cart lines are managed by dedicated cart-item endpoints. If the customer has no cart, the created cart should be empty and ready for later item additions. Return the full cart entity after creation or retrieval. Use a transaction if the implementation needs to create the cart and preload related summary data atomically.

The cart is a one-to-one record for each customer account, and each cart item references a single product variant. Item-level information is used to present subtotal and availability warnings, while overall cart totals are derived from the current cart contents. If the cart does not exist, does not belong to the caller, or has been removed, the request must be rejected.

Do not expose carts belonging to other customers. If the cart is missing, deleted, or inaccessible due to ownership rules, return a not-found or forbidden-style failure according to the service convention. The endpoint is read-only and must not recalculate or mutate inventory, quantities, or availability state during retrieval; it should only reflect the persisted cart state and the current referenced variant data.

operations.description:
Update a customer shopping cart.

This operation modifies the active cart that belongs to the authenticated customer and returns the refreshed cart state after the change. The cart header is the ownership boundary for the customer's pending purchase state, while the actual selected variants and quantities are stored in cart item rows.

When the cart is updated, the service must preserve the customer-to-cart ownership rule, validate that the cart belongs to the caller, and reconcile the cart contents against the referenced product variants. If cart items are adjusted, the resulting cart must reflect the current line items, availability state, and any recalculated totals derived from the normalized cart item records.

If the request cannot be completed because the cart does not exist, does not belong to the customer, or contains invalid/unavailable variants, the operation must fail without partially changing the cart. The response returns the full updated cart representation for use in checkout and cart review flows.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the target shopping cart by UUID and verify it belongs to the authenticated customer. Reject access when the cart is missing or owned by another customer.

Apply the update inside a transaction. Because the schema for mall_platform_shopping_carts contains only ownership and lifecycle fields, treat this endpoint as a cart reconciliation operation rather than a simple scalar-field patch. Use the existing cart and its cart items as the source of truth, then update the cart aggregate consistently.

If the request includes cart item changes, validate each referenced product variant exists, is active, and is purchasable. Ensure quantities are positive integers. When the same variant appears more than once in the requested cart state, merge quantities into a single cart item row to preserve the unique constraint on (shopping_cart_id, product_variant_id). If an existing cart item is updated, modify that row instead of creating duplicates.

Recompute availability_state for each affected cart item from the current product variant state and stock context. If a variant is deleted, inactive, or unavailable, mark the item accordingly and do not allow checkout-ready state for that line. Preserve other untouched cart items unless the request explicitly replaces the cart contents.

After successful reconciliation, persist the cart and affected cart items, update timestamps, and return the complete cart entity. On any validation or persistence failure, roll back the transaction so no partial cart changes remain.

This operation permanently removes the shopping cart header from active use, including the cart state used during checkout preparation. It is intended for authenticated customers deleting their own cart, and the server must confirm that the cart belongs to the current customer before performing the deletion.

Because cart items are subordinate to the cart, deleting the cart also removes its contained line items from active use. If the cart cannot be found or does not belong to the caller, the request must be rejected without affecting any other saved cart or customer data.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the shopping cart by cartId and verify ownership against the authenticated customer account.
If the cart does not exist, return not found. If the cart exists but belongs to another customer, return forbidden or not found according to the project error policy.
Delete the cart record and its dependent cart items in a single transactional operation so no orphaned cart lines remain.
Do not modify unrelated customer data, wishlist data, orders, or saved addresses.
If the cart is already absent, treat the request as a not found case and do not create any side effects.

parameters.description: Shopping cart identifier in the current customer scope.
parameters.name: cartId

operations.description:
Update the items contained in a shopping cart.

This operation lets an authenticated customer modify the contents of one cart they own, including changing the selected product variant line and adjusting item quantity for checkout preparation. Cart items are independent lines, so updates must only affect the targeted item or variant combination and must not merge, overwrite, or alter other lines in the cart.

The cart is the customer-owned container for selected variant lines before checkout. The service must validate cart ownership, verify the referenced variant exists and is purchasable, and ensure quantity changes respect current stock and cart rules. If an update cannot be completed, the previously saved cart contents must remain unchanged for the unaffected items.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the target shopping cart by cart ID and confirm it belongs to the authenticated customer. Reject access when the cart is not owned by the caller or is unavailable.

Apply the requested cart item changes as a partial update to the cart item collection. For each requested line, locate the existing cart item by variant or line identity as defined by the request DTO, then update quantity and any allowed item attributes. When the request introduces a variant already present in the cart, combine quantities instead of creating a duplicate line. Preserve all other cart items unchanged.

Validate that each referenced product variant exists, is active, and can be purchased. Check current stock before accepting quantity increases; if the requested quantity exceeds stock, reject the change for that item and leave the rest of the cart intact. If a variant is deleted, unavailable, or otherwise cannot be used, mark or reject only that affected line according to business rules without mutating unrelated lines.

Recalculate per-item subtotal values and the cart total after successful changes. Persist the cart item rows and any derived cart totals in a single transaction so a failed item update does not partially modify the cart state. Return a paginated cart-item summary payload if the implementation models the cart items as a searchable collection; otherwise return the updated cart item collection summary. Emit validation errors for missing ownership, invalid variant references, non-positive quantities, and stock violations.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of cart item summaries after applying the requested update, reflecting the cart contents currently stored for the authenticated customer.

parameters.description: Identifier of the shopping cart to update (scoped to the authenticated customer).
parameters.name: cartId

requestBody.description: Requested cart item changes, including quantity adjustments and variant-line updates for the specified shopping cart.

prerequisites.description: The referenced product variant must already exist and be purchasable before it can be added to or updated in a customer cart.

operations.description:
Create a new item in a shopping cart.

This operation adds a selected product variant to the specified customer cart and records the requested quantity as a single cart line. If the same variant already exists in the cart, the service should merge the quantities instead of creating a duplicate line, preserving the unique cart-and-variant relationship stored in the cart item table.

The cart item is used for checkout preparation and availability validation. The selected variant must belong to a real product variant record, and the cart must belong to the authenticated customer who is allowed to manage it. Quantity changes affect downstream subtotal and total calculations, while availability state must reflect the current stock or variant status so the cart can warn about unavailable or insufficiently stocked items.
operations.name: postByCartid
operations.specification:
Load the target cart by cartId and verify it belongs to the authenticated customer. Reject the request if the cart does not exist or is not accessible.

Validate the requested product variant exists and is eligible for cart usage. The cart item row stores only the selected variant, quantity, and availability state; it must not duplicate product-level data. Enforce the cart-item uniqueness constraint on (shopping cart, product variant): if a matching row already exists, update its quantity by adding the incoming quantity instead of inserting a second row.

When creating or merging the item, determine availability_state from the current variant state and available stock. If stock is insufficient or the variant is inactive/deleted, still preserve the line item only if business rules permit cart retention, and mark availability accordingly so checkout validation can block purchase later. Recalculate cart totals at read time or through cart aggregation logic after persistence.

Reject non-positive quantities and handle concurrent updates safely to avoid duplicate rows for the same cart and variant. Use a transaction when checking for an existing line and inserting/updating it. Return the created or merged cart item with its current state. Do not modify other cart lines.

responseBody.description: The cart item that was created or merged into the cart, including its current quantity and availability state.

parameters.description: Identifier of the shopping cart owned by the authenticated customer.
parameters.name: cartId

requestBody.description: Details required to add a product variant to the cart.

prerequisites.description: A shopping cart container must exist before a cart item can be added to it.
The chosen product variant must exist as a valid sellable variant resource before it can be referenced by the cart item.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single item from a shopping cart.

This endpoint returns the cart line that belongs to the specified shopping cart, including the selected product variant, quantity, and current availability state used during checkout validation. It is intended for cart detail screens and other flows that need to inspect one line item in its full context.

The returned cart item is scoped to the parent cart, so the requested cart and cart item identifiers must match an existing parent-child relationship. The item remains visible even when the referenced variant is unavailable, allowing the customer to understand what must be resolved before checkout.

If the cart or cart item does not exist, or if the item does not belong to the specified cart, the operation must return an appropriate not-found response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the cart item by cart ID and cart item ID, ensuring the item belongs to the requested cart. Query mall_platform_cart_items by id and mall_platform_shopping_cart_id, and include the related productVariant and shoppingCart relations if the implementation returns composed entity data.

Validate that the cart is owned by the authenticated customer before returning data. If the item is missing or belongs to a different cart, return not found rather than leaking cross-cart existence. Preserve the stored quantity and availability_state exactly as persisted, since unavailable items must still be visible in the cart.

No mutation occurs. Do not calculate checkout eligibility here; only return the current persisted item state and related product variant context required by the UI.

responseBody.description: The shopping cart item and its related context.

parameters.description: Identifier of the shopping cart that owns the item.
parameters.name: cartId

parameters.description: Identifier of the cart item within the specified cart.

operations.description:
Update a cart item within a customer shopping cart.

This operation changes the selected product variant and quantity for one existing cart line while keeping the cart scoped to its parent shopping cart. The cart item belongs to exactly one cart, and the selected variant must reference an existing product variant that can be represented in the cart.

The service must validate that the cart item belongs to the specified cart, that the referenced variant is active and available for cart use, and that the resulting quantity is positive. If the same variant already exists in the cart, the update logic should merge the quantities according to cart rules instead of creating duplicate lines. When validation fails, the cart item and the rest of the cart must remain unchanged.
operations.name: putByCartidAndCartitemid
operations.specification:
Load the shopping cart by cartId and verify ownership through the authenticated customer context. Then load the cart item by cartItemId and ensure it belongs to that cart; reject the request if the item is missing or scoped to a different cart.

Apply updates transactionally. If the request changes the product variant, validate the target mall_platform_product_variants row exists, is active, and can be added to cart. If the target variant already exists as another cart line in the same cart, merge quantities into that existing line and delete or replace the current line according to the cart service rule for unique cart lines per variant. If only quantity changes, update the existing row directly.

Enforce quantity > 0 and preserve the cart's non-duplicated variant rule from the unique constraint on (mall_platform_shopping_cart_id, mall_platform_product_variant_id). Recalculate availability state from the current variant state and stock conditions if the service maintains that field during cart updates. Use a transaction so partial updates cannot occur; on any validation or persistence failure, roll back all changes and return an error without altering other cart items.

Return the updated cart item with its parent cart and variant references intact. Do not modify unrelated cart items.

responseBody.description: The updated cart item after applying the requested changes.

parameters.description: Identifier of the shopping cart that owns the item.

operations.description:
Remove one item from a shopping cart.

This operation deletes a specific cart line for the authenticated customer and updates the cart state accordingly. The removed entry is no longer shown in the cart view, and the cart total is recalculated after the deletion.

The cart item is scoped to the owning shopping cart, so both `{cartId}` and `{cartItemId}` are required to identify the target line precisely. If the requested item is no longer present, the request is handled safely and the remaining cart contents are left unchanged.

Because cart items are tied to a customer-owned shopping cart and reference a single product variant, the service must verify ownership before removal and reject cross-account access with an authorization or not-found style error as appropriate.
operations.name: eraseByCartidAndCartitemid
operations.specification:
Load the shopping cart by cartId and verify it belongs to the authenticated customer. Then locate the cart item by cartItemId within that cart. If the item exists, delete only that cart line and recalculate the cart total from the remaining cart items. If the item is missing, treat the request as safe no-op behavior and return success without modifying other cart items.

Do not allow removal of an item from another customer's cart. If the cart itself does not belong to the caller, return an authorization or not-found error according to platform conventions. Use a transaction so the item removal and any derived cart-total updates remain consistent. No snapshot is required for cart-item removal unless the platform has a separate audit mechanism for cart edits.

parameters.description: Identifier of the shopping cart that owns the cart item. This scope is required to ensure the item is removed from the correct customer cart.
parameters.name: cartId

parameters.description: Identifier of the cart item within the specified shopping cart.

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated customer's wishlist as a paginated list of saved products.

This operation provides the customer-facing browsing view for products the customer has marked for later interest. Each result represents one saved product entry and is intended to support discovery and return visits to previously considered products.

The list reflects the customer's own saved items only. Products that were deleted from the catalog are no longer shown because wishlist maintenance keeps saved references aligned with products that still exist. The response is suitable for wishlist pages that need pagination, sorting, and current product summaries.

If the request references unavailable paging or sorting combinations, the service must reject the request with a validation error. If the customer's wishlist has no items, an empty page should be returned rather than an error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the authenticated customer context and resolve that customer's wishlist container and wishlist items. Query wishlist items joined to current product rows, and exclude items whose referenced product no longer exists or is no longer eligible for browsing. Return a paginated projection of saved products suitable for UI display.

Implement paging, search, and sorting in the request body. Paging must be stable and deterministic. Sorting should default to a sensible customer browsing order if not supplied, and should support product-centric ordering fields used by wishlist pages. Do not expose wishlist entries belonging to any other customer.

If the wishlist container is missing for the authenticated customer, return an empty page rather than failing. If related product data has been removed, omit those rows from the result set. Preserve atomic read behavior and do not mutate any wishlist data in this operation.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of the authenticated customer's wishlist product summaries.

requestBody.description: Wishlist browsing criteria including pagination, search, and sorting options for the authenticated customer.

operations.description:
Retrieve the current wishlist for a registered customer.

A wishlist is a customer-owned container that stores saved products for later browsing and purchase consideration. This operation returns one wishlist in full detail so the owner can review the products they have saved and continue browsing their personal saved-item list.

The response is limited to the authenticated customer who owns the wishlist. If the wishlist does not exist, belongs to another customer, or the requester is not a registered customer, the request must fail with an appropriate access or not-found error. Deleted products should not appear as saved items in the returned wishlist.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the wishlist row by wishlistId and verify it belongs to the authenticated customer account.
Join or populate the wishlist's saved product items from mall_platform_wishlist_items, and for each saved product ensure the referenced product still exists and is visible according to catalog rules. Exclude any wishlist items whose products were deleted so the returned data matches current wishlist-maintenance expectations.

Do not allow access for non-customer actors or for customers requesting another customer's wishlist. Return 404 when the wishlist does not exist or is not owned by the caller, and return 403 only when the caller is authenticated but lacks customer access. The operation is read-only and must not mutate wishlist rows or wishlist items.

responseBody.description: The full wishlist owned by the customer, including its current saved product composition.

parameters.description: The wishlist identifier in the customer's scope.
parameters.name: wishlistId

operations.description:
Save a product to the authenticated customer’s wishlist.

This operation creates one saved-product entry linked to the customer’s wishlist so the customer can revisit the product later. Wishlist entries are stored at the product level, not the variant level, and the underlying wishlist item table enforces one entry per customer and product combination.

If the same product is already saved, the service should not create a duplicate row. The product must exist and be available for saving at the time of the request. When the product is deleted, related wishlist entries are removed automatically by the database relationships.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Validate that the caller is an authenticated customer and resolve the customer-owned wishlist container. Reject requests from non-customer actors.

Insert a wishlist item for the requested product only after verifying that the product exists and is currently saveable. Enforce uniqueness so the same customer cannot create duplicate wishlist entries for the same product; if the item already exists, return the existing state or a conflict according to service conventions, but do not duplicate rows.

Use the mall_platform_wishlists parent/container concept and mall_platform_wishlist_items child record. Do not modify the product itself. If the product has been deleted or is otherwise unavailable for saving, return a validation error. Keep the operation atomic so the wishlist is unchanged on failure.

responseBody.description: The saved wishlist item linked to the customer’s wishlist and the selected product.

requestBody.description: The product to save in the authenticated customer’s wishlist.

operations.description:
Update the products saved in a customer's wishlist.

This operation lets a signed-in customer manage their personal wishlist, which stores saved products for later consideration. Wishlist entries are product-level items, so each saved row represents a product rather than a specific variant or option combination.

The service must verify that the wishlist belongs to the authenticated customer, enforce customer-only access, and preserve the existing saved products if the update cannot be completed. Deleted products must not remain in the wishlist, and the final saved list must remain consistent with the unique relationship between a wishlist and its products.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the wishlist by id and verify that it belongs to the authenticated customer. Reconcile the wishlist item set according to the request body using the wishlist_items table, preserving the wishlist header row. Enforce the unique [wishlist_id, product_id] constraint so each product appears at most once. Reject or ignore product ids that do not exist or have been deleted, depending on the request contract used by the implementation layer, but never leave the wishlist in a partially updated state.

Implement the update transactionally: compute the target product set, delete removed wishlist items, insert newly added ones, and leave existing items intact when still selected. Because deleted products are automatically removed from wishlists, the service should also filter out orphaned saved products before committing. Update the wishlist timestamp on success. If any validation or persistence error occurs, roll back the entire change so the customer's saved list remains unchanged.

Return the updated wishlist representation after persistence. Use customer-only authorization and ensure the path wishlist id is sufficient for lookup; do not duplicate path parameters in the request body.

responseBody.description: The updated customer wishlist after the saved product set has been applied.

parameters.description: The wishlist identifier for the customer's own wishlist.
parameters.name: wishlistId

requestBody.description: The desired set of product-level saved items for the authenticated customer's wishlist.

operations.description:
Permanently removes the authenticated customer’s wishlist container.

This operation deletes the saved wishlist list for a customer account. The wishlist is the container that groups saved products, while the individual saved entries are stored as wishlist items. Removing the wishlist also removes its saved entries so the customer no longer keeps a saved-product list for future browsing.

The operation is customer-scoped and must only affect the wishlist owned by the current authenticated customer. If the wishlist does not exist or does not belong to the caller, the request must be rejected. Related product records are not modified by this operation, and catalog data remains unchanged.

If the wishlist has already been removed, the implementation should return a not-found style error rather than creating a replacement record. Any dependent wishlist items must be deleted within the same transaction so partial cleanup cannot occur.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the wishlist by wishlistId and verify that it belongs to the authenticated customer account. Reject access if the wishlist is owned by another customer or if the caller is unauthenticated.

Delete dependent mall_platform_wishlist_items rows for the wishlist first, then delete the mall_platform_wishlists row in a single transaction to avoid orphaned items. Use the actual foreign-key relationship from the schema; do not modify mall_platform_products or any product-related records.

If the wishlist does not exist, return a not-found error. If ownership does not match, return a forbidden or not-found style error according to the platform’s authorization pattern. The operation should be idempotent from a client perspective only if the platform standard treats repeated deletions as not found; otherwise preserve strict not-found behavior.

parameters.description: Identifier of the wishlist to remove (global scope).
parameters.name: wishlistId

operations.description:
Retrieve and manage the saved product entries inside a wishlist.

This operation returns the wishlist’s product-level saved items for the owning customer account. Wishlist entries are maintained as references to products that still exist in the catalog, so the list reflects the customer’s current saved-product interest and can be used to revisit products later.

The endpoint is also used for wishlist browsing with pagination and filtering. It should only expose items that belong to the specified wishlist and must respect product visibility rules, including automatic removal of entries whose products have been deleted. If a saved product no longer exists, it must not appear in the returned list.

If a request cannot be completed because the wishlist does not exist or the caller is not authorized to access it, the service must return the appropriate not-found or forbidden response. Failed operations must not partially modify the saved list.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the wishlist by wishlistId and verify it belongs to the current authenticated customer. Reject access if the wishlist does not exist or is not owned by the caller.

Query wishlist item rows for that wishlist, joining to the referenced products to ensure the saved product still exists. Exclude any wishlist item whose product has been deleted so browsing never exposes stale entries. Because wishlist items are product-level references, return product-oriented summaries rather than variant-level details.

Support request-body-driven pagination, sorting, and any allowed product/search filters defined by the wishlist browsing requirements. Order results deterministically, and return a paginated response wrapper.

If a saved product is missing, omit it from the result set rather than failing the request. Do not mutate data during this read operation. If an implementation also supports bulk maintenance through this endpoint, ensure removals are atomic per request and preserve remaining wishlist items unchanged on failure.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of the wishlist’s saved product entries.

parameters.description: The wishlist identifier in the customer's account scope.
parameters.name: wishlistId

requestBody.description: Pagination, sorting, and filtering criteria for browsing wishlist items.

operations.description:
Add a product to a customer's wishlist.

This operation creates one saved-product entry under the specified wishlist so the customer can keep track of products they want to revisit later. Wishlist items are stored at the product level only, which means the saved entry represents interest in the product itself rather than a specific variant.

The created wishlist item is scoped to the given wishlist and must not duplicate an existing saved product in the same wishlist. If the same product is already present, the request should be rejected as a duplicate rather than creating another row. If the product no longer exists, the operation must fail because wishlist browsing must only contain current catalog products.

This endpoint is intended for the customer who owns the wishlist. It supports the wishlist browsing experience by preserving saved items in a paginated collection and automatically aligns with wishlist maintenance rules when products are removed elsewhere in the system.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target wishlist by id and verify it belongs to the current authenticated customer. Reject the request if the wishlist does not exist or the caller is not allowed to manage it.

Validate that the referenced product exists and is currently available for saving. Because the table stores only wishlist-to-product links, create a single mall_platform_wishlist_items row using the parent wishlist id from the path and the product id from the request body.

Before insert, check the unique constraint on (mall_platform_wishlist_id, mall_platform_product_id) to prevent duplicates. If the pair already exists, return a conflict-style error and do not modify any other rows.

Use a transaction for the existence check and insert to avoid race conditions. Populate created_at and updated_at from the persistence layer. Do not invent extra fields, because the schema only contains wishlist, product, timestamps, and deleted_at. If the product has been deleted by another process, fail cleanly and leave the wishlist unchanged.

responseBody.description: The created wishlist item with its identifier, ownership links, and timestamps.

requestBody.description: Product reference to save in the specified wishlist.

operations.description:
Retrieve one saved product entry from a customer wishlist.

This operation returns a single wishlist item belonging to the specified wishlist, including the saved product reference that customers marked for later review. Wishlist items are maintained at the product level, so the result reflects one saved product entry rather than a variant-level cart line.

The wishlist belongs to one customer account, and this endpoint must verify that the requested wishlist item exists within that wishlist before returning it. If the item does not belong to the given wishlist, or if either record cannot be found, the service should respond with a not-found error. If the saved product was removed from the catalog, the item should no longer be returned because wishlist maintenance keeps saved products aligned with existing catalog data.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the wishlist by wishlistId, then fetch the wishlist item by wishlistItemId constrained to that wishlist. Join or include the linked product so the caller can confirm which product was saved.

Enforce ownership through the wishlist parent relationship: only the owning customer should be allowed to access the item. Return a single record, not a collection. If the wishlist item does not exist under the given wishlist, return a 404-style not found response.

Because wishlist items are deleted automatically when products are deleted, there is no need to special-case missing product rows beyond not returning orphaned entries. Do not expose unrelated wishlist items from the same customer or any other customer.

responseBody.description: The saved product entry currently stored in the specified wishlist.

operations.description:
Remove a product from a customer wishlist.

This operation deletes one saved product entry from the specified wishlist while leaving the underlying product record unchanged. It is intended for customer-facing wishlist maintenance, allowing shoppers to keep their saved items list focused on products they still want to revisit.

If the requested wishlist item no longer exists, the operation still succeeds without affecting the remaining wishlist contents. This also aligns with platform cleanup behavior when a product has already been removed from the catalog and automatically cleared from wishlists. The wishlist itself remains available for other saved items, and no other customer data is changed.

Errors are returned only when the wishlist scope is invalid, the item does not belong to the specified wishlist, or the requester is not authorized to modify that wishlist.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the target wishlist item by wishlistId and wishlistItemId with ownership validation for the current customer.
Verify the item belongs to the referenced wishlist before deletion to prevent cross-wishlist removal.
Perform a single delete operation against mall_platform_wishlist_items. If the row is already missing, treat the operation as successful and return the post-delete response shape without error.
Do not modify mall_platform_wishlists or mall_platform_products.
Ensure the operation is idempotent and preserves the rest of the wishlist unchanged.
Return an appropriate not-found or forbidden error only when the wishlist context is invalid or the caller lacks ownership.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of the authenticated customer's orders.

This endpoint is used to browse order history and search past purchases. Each returned order reflects the customer-owned checkout record stored in the order header, including the order number, total amount, creation time, and the derived overall order status computed from its order items.

The list is intended for customer order history screens, so results must be paginated and sorted by newest first by default. Filtering and search should respect the authenticated customer scope and never expose orders belonging to other customers. Related order-item, shipment, and preserved shipping-address details are available through the corresponding order detail endpoint.

If the requested page is out of range or the criteria match no orders, the response should still be a valid empty page. Any invalid filter or sort option must be rejected with a business validation error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_orders for the authenticated customer only.
Apply pagination, newest-first default sorting, and optional search/filter criteria from the request body.
Support filtering by order status and date range if provided by the request DTO. Do not expose orders from other customers.
Use the derived overall order status stored on the order row, which is computed from related order items by business rules. Include total_amount and created_at in summary output, and order_number for identification.
Return a paginated list of summary records ordered consistently. If no rows match, return an empty page rather than an error. Validate request sort fields and filter enums strictly; reject unknown criteria. Do not join heavy nested data such as full order items or shipments in this endpoint.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of customer order summaries.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, sort, and pagination criteria for customer order history.

operations.description:
Retrieve the full details of a single order for the authenticated customer.

This endpoint returns one order record together with the preserved purchase context needed to display the order detail page, including the item list, item statuses, shipping address, and shipment information. It is intended for customers opening an order from their own order history, where the platform shows the complete checkout result and the per-item progress of the purchase.

The returned order must include the item-level history that captures the product name, variant, quantity, price, and status for each purchased line. It must also expose shipment tracking data when shipments exist, so the customer can review delivery progress for each seller-specific package. If the order does not belong to the current customer, the service must reject the request rather than exposing another customer's purchase history.

Because this is a money-related record, the response must preserve historical values exactly as stored on the order and order-item snapshot records. Any missing order ID, unauthorized access, or nonexistent order should result in an appropriate not-found or forbidden response from the service layer.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the order by its identifier for the authenticated customer only.
Join or hydrate the related order items, item snapshots, shipment records, shipment items, and preserved shipping address so the consumer receives the complete detail view in one call.

Enforce ownership validation before returning data: the requested order must belong to the current customer account unless the caller has an administrative override permission. If the caller is a customer, reject access to any order that belongs to another customer.

Return the preserved order data exactly as recorded at checkout time. Do not reconstruct historical product or seller values from current product tables; use the stored snapshot rows for item names, variant options, prices, and seller profile presentation.

If the order is not found, return a not-found error. If ownership validation fails, return a forbidden error. If related shipment data is absent, return the order with an empty shipment collection rather than failing the request.

responseBody.description: Full order details including item history, shipping address, and shipment tracking information.

parameters.description: The order identifier within the customer's own order history.
parameters.name: orderId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of order items for a specific order.

This operation returns the item-level history for one order, including each purchased product variant, quantity, price, and current item status. It supports the order detail experience for customers and also provides the operational item view used by sellers and administrators for shipping, cancellation review, refund review, and dispute handling.

The result is always restricted to the order identified by the path parameter. Access control must ensure that customers can only view their own orders, sellers can only view items belonging to their own products within the order, and administrators can view any order item as part of platform oversight. The response should preserve the preserved purchase context where available, including seller and product references captured for historical review.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load order items by orderId with pagination, search, and sorting support.
Use the order header as the mandatory scope filter and query mall_platform_order_items joined with preserved snapshot data when needed for summary fields such as product name, variant representation, seller shop name, item status, quantity, and price.

Apply authorization checks before querying:
- customer: only the owner of the order
- seller: only items that belong to the seller's own products
- administrator: all orders

Support filters that are appropriate for item browsing, such as item status and seller scope when the caller is a seller or administrator. Preserve ordering by newest or most relevant item state according to the request sort parameters. Return a paginated summary list, not full entity snapshots.

If the order does not exist, return not found. If the caller is not allowed to access the order, return forbidden. If pagination parameters are invalid, return validation errors. Do not expose items from other orders.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order item summaries for a single order.

parameters.description: The order identifier that scopes the item list.
parameters.name: orderId

requestBody.description: Search, pagination, and sorting criteria for listing items within the specified order.

operations.description:
Retrieve the full details of one purchased order item within an order.

This operation exposes the item-level history for a specific purchase line, including the purchased product variant, quantity, price, and current item status. It is intended to support customer order history views as well as seller and administrator dispute review workflows when they need to inspect a single line item in the context of its parent order.

The order item is always scoped by its parent order, and the system must ensure that the requested item belongs to the referenced order. Only the owning customer may access their own order items, while sellers and administrators may access the record when their permissions allow intervention or review. If the order, the order item, or the access scope does not match, the service must return the appropriate not-found or forbidden response.

Return the complete order item entity with its preserved purchased-item context. Use joins or equivalent relation loading to include the parent order reference and the purchased variant context required by the item detail view. Preserve the item's immutable purchase information and current status; do not recompute historical purchase data from mutable product tables.

If the order does not exist, the item does not belong to the order, or the caller is outside the allowed visibility scope, return a not-found or forbidden error consistent with the platform's access-control behavior. Because this is a read-only detail endpoint, no write transaction is needed.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of shipments with filtering and sorting options.

This operation is used to browse shipment records that package one or more order items from the same seller. Each shipment belongs to a single order and a single seller, and its shipment items represent the order-item assignments included in that package.

The returned list is intended for shipment tracking, order history grouping, and seller fulfillment workflows. Consumers can search by shipment status, order, seller, and time range to locate specific packages and follow their tracking progress.

When no matching shipments are found, the response returns an empty page. Invalid filters or pagination values must be rejected with a validation error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_shipments as the base table and join mall_platform_orders, mall_platform_sellers, and mall_platform_shipment_items as needed for filtering and summary composition.
Support pagination, keyword-like filtering on tracking-related identifiers, and sorting by created_at or shipped_at in descending or ascending order as appropriate.
Respect seller-grouping rules by never mixing shipment items from different sellers in the same shipment summary. If a shipment has no shipment items yet, still return the shipment itself if it matches filters.
Ensure deleted_at records are excluded from normal browsing unless an explicit administrative recovery scenario is supported elsewhere. For customer-facing usage, scope results to shipments belonging to the authenticated customer through the related order.customer_id. For seller-facing usage, scope to the authenticated seller through mall_platform_seller_id.
Return a page of shipment summaries optimized for list display, including tracking metadata and the linked order number. Handle empty result sets cleanly and reject invalid page, size, or sort values.

operations.description:
Create a shipment for one seller's order items that still need shipping.

This operation records a seller-specific delivery package, captures the carrier and tracking number, and links the selected order items to that shipment. It supports the marketplace rule that items from different sellers must never be combined in the same package, while allowing one shipment to contain one or more eligible items from the same seller and order.

When the shipment is created, the system marks every included order item as shipped and preserves the shared tracking information for customer order history and delivery confirmation. The operation must reject items that already belong to another shipment, items that are no longer eligible for shipping, or item sets that mix multiple sellers or orders. Completed or unavailable shipment targets must not be recreated.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert one new row into mall_platform_shipments and related rows into mall_platform_shipment_items within a single transaction.

Validate that all requested order items exist, belong to the same seller account as the authenticated seller, belong to the same order when required by the business workflow, and are currently eligible for shipping. Reject the request if any item is already assigned to another active shipment, if any item is not in a shippable state, or if the selected items span multiple sellers. Use the order-item and shipment relationships to enforce seller grouping.

Persist the carrier name and tracking number on the shipment row. Create shipment-item associations for every included order item, then transition each order item status to shipped in the same transaction. If any validation or persistence step fails, roll back the entire shipment creation so no partial shipment or partial status update remains.

Return a full shipment entity with its linked items, and surface standard not-found, conflict, and validation errors when the order, items, or seller scope are invalid. Do not allow recreation of a shipment that has already been completed or any duplicate assignment of the same eligible item to another shipment.

responseBody.description: The newly created shipment with its included order items and tracking details.

requestBody.description: Shipment creation details including the selected order items and shared tracking information.

operations.description:
Retrieve the full details of a single shipment.

A shipment represents one seller-specific delivery package, including its carrier name, tracking number, optional tracking URL, shipping status, and shipment timestamps. The response is intended to support order history and fulfillment views where customers need to see how items were grouped for delivery and how to follow the package.

The shipment is linked to one order and one seller, and it contains one or more order items through shipment-item assignments. Consumers can use this operation to inspect the shipment header together with the items included in the package, while preserving the seller separation rule that items from different sellers are never combined into the same shipment.

If the shipment does not exist or is not accessible to the current actor, the service should return a not-found or forbidden response according to platform authorization rules. Deleted or unavailable shipment records must not be exposed in this detail view.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the shipment by its UUID primary key with its related seller, order, and shipmentItems/orderItem graph.
Return a single shipment detail DTO that includes carrier_name, tracking_number, tracking_url, status, shipped_at, delivered_at, created_at, updated_at, plus the linked order and the list of included order items.
Use the shipment_items junction table to enumerate membership and ensure the items belong to the same shipment. Preserve the order-item relational fields needed by downstream consumers, including product variant and seller references when composing the response.
Authorize access so customers can only read shipments belonging to their own order history, while sellers can only read shipments for orders containing their items. Administrators may read any shipment.
Reject missing records with not found. If the shipment has been removed or is otherwise unavailable, return not found rather than a partial payload.

responseBody.description: Full shipment details including tracking data and included order items.

operations.description:
Update an existing shipment's tracking and status information.

This operation lets an authorized seller revise the shipment header used to group order items from the same seller. The shipment record stores the shared carrier name, tracking number, optional tracking URL, and current shipment status, so updates here affect every order item assigned to that shipment.

Shipment updates are part of the seller fulfillment workflow and customer delivery flow. When the shipment reaches a delivered state, the system should record the delivery timestamp and keep the shipment-item grouping intact for order history and dispute review. If the shipment is already completed or otherwise unavailable for further shipping actions, the request must be rejected without altering the existing shipment data.

Validation should ensure the shipment exists, belongs to the caller's allowed scope, and remains eligible for update. Invalid carrier or tracking information, status transitions that conflict with the current shipment state, and attempts to modify unavailable shipments must return appropriate errors.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the shipment by id and verify access permissions for the caller. Update only shipment header fields that are allowed by the update DTO: carrier_name, tracking_number, tracking_url, and status. Do not modify shipment-item memberships in this endpoint; shipment contents are managed through the shipment-item relation separately.

Enforce business constraints from fulfillment rules. A shipment belongs to one seller and one order, so ensure the caller is permitted to manage that seller's shipment. Reject updates to shipments that are already completed or otherwise unavailable for shipping actions. If the new status represents delivery completion, set delivered_at accordingly; if the shipment transitions to shipped, set shipped_at if not already present. Preserve existing timestamps when the state does not require them.

Validate that tracking_number remains unique within the seller scope if the database constraint applies, and return a conflict-style error on duplicate tracking data. Keep the operation transactional so partial updates do not occur. If any validation fails, no fields should be persisted.

responseBody.description: The updated shipment record with carrier, tracking, status, and timestamps.

parameters.description: Shipment identifier (UUID).
parameters.name: shipmentId

operations.description:
Remove a shipment from an order fulfillment record.

A shipment represents one seller's delivery package and groups one or more order items that belong to the same seller. This operation lets the responsible seller remove a shipment record while keeping the associated order items and order history intact for customer service, tracking, and dispute review.

The service must validate that the shipment exists, that the requester is allowed to manage it, and that deleting the shipment will not violate shipment lifecycle rules. If the shipment is linked to order items that have already progressed beyond a removable state, the request must fail. When the shipment is removed, the underlying order items remain part of the order and continue to be visible in order history with their existing statuses and preserved snapshots where applicable.

If the shipment cannot be found, is not owned by the caller, or is in a state that prevents removal, the API must return an appropriate error without altering the order or item records.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the shipment by shipmentId and verify it exists. Confirm the caller has permission to manage the shipment, typically the owning seller or an administrator, according to the authorization middleware.

Before deleting, validate the shipment is still removable under shipment workflow rules. Because shipments group order items from the same seller, the implementation must not modify order items, order status calculations, or preserved snapshots. Only the shipment header and its linkage rows should be removed. If the schema stores shipment-item association rows separately, delete those association rows first or use a transaction with cascading behavior to keep referential integrity.

Do not touch inventory, order item statuses, cancellation/refund records, or order snapshots. Return the deleted shipment record as confirmation so the client can update shipment grouping in order detail views. If the shipment does not exist, return not found. If the caller is not permitted or the shipment is not deletable, return a validation or conflict error without partial changes.

parameters.description: The shipment identifier to remove.
parameters.name: shipmentId

operations.description:
Retrieve the order items that belong to a specific shipment.

A shipment is the package delivery unit for the marketplace and always represents items from one seller only. This operation exposes the items grouped inside that shipment so customers can understand which purchases travel together and so shipment-related views can present tracking context alongside the shipped items.

The returned list is suitable for order history and shipment detail screens. Each item should reflect the preserved order-item state at shipment time, including the product and variant context needed to identify the purchased line. If the shipment contains multiple items, they are returned together under the same shipment scope.

Validation errors must be raised when the shipment does not exist or when the caller is not allowed to view that shipment. The service must also reject any attempt to access items outside the shipment scope, and it must preserve the one-seller-per-shipment rule when loading related data.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the shipment by shipmentId, then query mall_platform_shipment_items joined with mall_platform_order_items for the shipment's order-item lines. Enforce that all returned items belong to the requested shipment and that the shipment itself contains only items from a single seller.

Apply pagination, search, and sorting through the request body. Search should operate on shipment item friendly fields derived from the related order-item snapshot context, such as product name, variant identity, and item status if those fields are exposed in the summary type. Keep the query scoped to the shipment to prevent cross-shipment leakage.

If the shipment does not exist, return a not-found error. If the caller is a customer, ensure the shipment is part of one of the customer's orders. If the caller is a seller, ensure the seller owns the shipment's seller scope. Do not expose items from other shipments or other sellers.

Return a paginated summary collection suitable for UI rendering. Use immutable shipment/order-item snapshot data where needed so the consumer sees stable purchase-time context rather than mutable live product data.

responseBody.description: Paginated shipment item summaries for the requested shipment.

operations.description:
Attach one or more eligible order items to an existing shipment.

A shipment is the physical package sent by one seller, and all items added through this operation must belong to that same seller and must be eligible for shipping. This endpoint supports seller fulfillment by letting the seller group one or more order items into the shipment that will carry shared tracking information.

The system must validate that the shipment exists, belongs to the authenticated seller, and is still in a state that allows item assignment. It must also reject items that are already assigned to another active shipment, belong to a different seller, or are not in a shippable status. If any item cannot be added, the request should fail without creating a partial shipment composition so the shipment remains internally consistent.

On success, the shipment-item links are created and the shipment composition is returned so clients can immediately display the updated package contents and tracking context. Related shipment and order views should reflect the new grouping. Authorization errors, not-found errors, and business-rule violations must be reported clearly when the shipment does not belong to the caller or the selected items are ineligible.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target shipment by shipmentId and verify it exists.
Validate that the authenticated seller owns the shipment through the shipment's seller relationship, and reject access if the shipment does not belong to the seller or if the caller is not permitted to manage shipments.

Parse the request body as the shipment-item create DTO. Resolve each referenced order item and verify all of the following before any insert occurs: the order item exists, belongs to the same seller as the shipment, is in a shippable state, and is not already assigned to another active shipment. If the shipment is already finalized or otherwise immutable, reject the operation.

Perform the creation in a transaction. Insert shipment-item association rows for all validated items, then update the affected order items to shipped status if that is part of the domain workflow for shipment creation in this endpoint's lifecycle. If the shipment creation flow elsewhere already marks items as shipped, avoid duplicating the status transition here and only maintain the association records.

If any selected order item fails validation, abort the whole transaction and return a business error describing the first blocking condition. Do not allow cross-seller item mixing, duplicate assignment, or partial attachment. After commit, reload the shipment with its items and related order-item details for the response payload.

The response is intended for shipment detail screens and order detail views. It should include the shipment-item record itself and the references needed to understand which shipment and order item are associated with it. If the shipment or item does not exist, or if the item does not belong to the specified shipment, the request must fail with a not-found response.

Load the shipment item by shipment ID and shipment item ID in a single lookup. Verify that the shipment item belongs to the requested shipment before returning it; if the shipment mismatch is detected, return not found rather than exposing cross-shipment data. Join the shipment item to its shipment and order item references as needed for the response payload.

Use the shipment scope as a mandatory parent filter because shipment items are subordinate to shipments and shipments are seller-specific. Do not allow retrieval when the shipment has been deleted or when the item is detached from the shipment. Return a 404 when either identifier is invalid, the shipment does not exist, or the item does not belong to that shipment.

operations.description:
Update a shipment-item assignment within a seller-specific shipment.

This operation changes which order item is associated with a shipment, allowing fulfillment staff to correct or adjust shipment membership when the shipment still contains eligible items from the same seller. The shipment remains the package-level container for shared carrier and tracking data, while the shipment-item relation records which purchased order item belongs to that package.

A shipment may contain one or more order items, but all items in the shipment must belong to the same seller. Each order item can belong to only one shipment at a time, so the service must reject updates that would move an order item into a second shipment or break the seller boundary. If the requested order item is already linked elsewhere, or if the shipment and order item do not match, the operation must fail with a conflict or validation error.

The response returns the updated shipment-item relationship. Because this endpoint operates on fulfillment data used for order tracking and delivery confirmation, access must be restricted to the shipment owner seller or an administrator, and the service should verify the referenced shipment and order item both exist and belong to the expected order context before applying the change.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the shipment-item row by shipmentItemId and ensure it belongs to shipmentId. Also load the shipment and the referenced order item to verify consistency.

Validate that the shipment exists, is not deleted, and belongs to the current seller or authorized administrator. Validate that the order item exists, is not deleted, and belongs to the same seller as the shipment. If the update changes the linked order item, ensure the target order item is eligible for the shipment, is not already assigned to another shipment, and does not violate the one-seller-per-shipment rule.

Apply the update in a transaction. If reassignment of the order item is supported, update the foreign key on mall_platform_shipment_items and preserve created_at while updating updated_at. If the design of the DTO does not support changing membership fields, implement the operation as a guarded no-op update that only refreshes timestamps; however, the endpoint should still reject any mismatch between the path shipmentId and the row's actual shipment.

Return the updated shipment-item relation after reloading it with shipment and orderItem references as needed by the response schema. Throw not found when the shipment-item row or shipment does not exist, conflict when the order item is already assigned elsewhere, and forbidden when the caller lacks seller ownership or admin privileges.

operations.description:
Remove one order item from a shipment.

This operation detaches a single shipment item from an existing shipment while preserving the shipment record itself. It is intended for seller-side shipping management where a shipment contains one or more order items from the same seller, and where shipment grouping must remain internally consistent.

The shipment item must belong to the specified shipment, and the shipment must remain valid after removal. If removing the item would leave the shipment empty, the service should either delete the shipment or reject the request according to shipment lifecycle rules defined by the shipment service. The operation should also keep order-item shipment relationships and shipment tracking data consistent for customer order detail views.

If the shipment or shipment item does not exist, or if the item is not part of the specified shipment, the service must return a not-found or validation error. If the shipment is already finalized and no longer editable, the service must reject the request with a business-rule error.
operations.name: erase
