Load the shipment by shipmentId and verify the shipmentItemId belongs to it. Confirm the caller is authorized to manage the shipment, typically the seller that owns the shipment or an administrator acting with oversight privileges. If the shipment item does not exist in that shipment, return a 404-style not found error.

Before removal, validate shipment editability according to shipment lifecycle rules. If the shipment is already shipped, delivered, or otherwise locked, reject the operation with a business-rule conflict. If shipment items are modeled through a join table, delete the join row only; do not alter the underlying order item record. If shipment item removal can empty the shipment, apply the service’s defined behavior consistently: either delete the shipment if empty shipments are not allowed, or reject the operation if at least one item must remain.

Keep shipment grouping by seller intact. Do not allow removal logic to move the order item into another seller’s shipment. After successful removal, persist changes in a transaction and update any derived shipment summaries or counts needed by order detail views. Return no body on success unless the project’s shared REST conventions require an acknowledgment payload.

operations.description:
Create a cancellation request for a single order item.

This operation lets a customer submit a cancellation reason for one purchased item when the item is still eligible for cancellation. The request is tied to the specific order item and starts a seller review workflow so the seller can approve or reject it later.

A cancellation request preserves the current request state, reviewer fields, and timestamps in the cancellation request record. The system must reject requests for items that are not in an eligible state, and it must not create duplicate cancellation requests for the same order item because each order item can have only one cancellation request.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target mall_platform_order_items row by id and ensure it exists and belongs to the current customer context.
Verify that the order item status is eligible for cancellation: it must be paid and not shipped, based on the business rules for item-level cancellation.
Check that no mall_platform_cancellation_requests row already exists for the same mall_platform_order_item_id because the schema enforces uniqueness and the business flow expects one request per item.
Create the cancellation request row with mall_platform_order_item_id from the path, reason from the request body, status set to pending, and reviewer-related columns left null: reviewer_id, reviewed_at, review_result, reviewer_note.
Set created_at and updated_at at insertion time. Do not change the order item status, inventory, or payment state at this step; those changes happen only after review approval.
If the item is missing, already shipped, already cancelled, or already has a cancellation request, return a business validation error and do not persist anything. Use a transaction so the uniqueness and eligibility checks remain consistent under concurrent requests.

operations.description:
Submit or update the cancellation request for one purchased order item.

This operation lets the customer explain why a single paid, unshipped order item should be cancelled. Cancellation is item-level, so the request applies only to the specified order item and does not affect other items in the same order. The seller responsible for that item reviews the request and decides whether to approve or reject it.

The request is only valid while the order item is still in paid status and has not yet been shipped. If the item is no longer eligible, the service must reject the request without changing the item, the order, or unrelated cancellation requests. When the request is accepted, the stored cancellation state should be available for later seller review and dispute handling.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the target order item by orderItemId and verify that it belongs to the authenticated customer, is in paid status, and has not been shipped. Reject the operation if the item does not exist, is not owned by the caller, or is no longer eligible for cancellation.

If a cancellation request already exists for the order item, update its reason and keep it tied to the same item. If no request exists yet, create the request record for that item. Persist the request using the cancellation request table and ensure the item-scoped relationship is preserved exactly one-to-one at the business level.

Do not change the order item status here; this endpoint only submits the customer’s cancellation request. The seller’s approval or rejection flow is handled elsewhere. If validation fails, return a business error and leave the existing order item and cancellation request state unchanged.

responseBody.description: The current cancellation request state for the specified order item after submission.

operations.description:

operations.description:
Update a cancellation request for a specific order item.

This operation is used when the seller of the order item, or an authorized administrator, reviews an existing cancellation request and records the decision and outcome details. Cancellation is handled at the order-item level, so the request remains scoped to one purchased item and does not affect the rest of the order unless the business rules later cause the entire order to become fully cancelled.

The request can only be updated while the underlying order item is still eligible for cancellation review. If the item is no longer in the correct paid and unshipped state, the request must be rejected with a business validation error. When the request is successfully updated, the system must preserve the prior state in a snapshot so the review history remains available for dispute resolution and auditing.

operations.specification:
Load the cancellation request by both orderItemId and cancellationRequestId to ensure it belongs to the specified order item.

Validate that the authenticated actor is the seller of the order item or an administrator with permission to review cancellation requests. Confirm that the target order item exists and that the cancellation request exists, is linked to that order item, and is in an updatable state.

Apply the update using a transaction. If the review approves the request, transition the cancellation request to approved and cancel the order item, then create the necessary inventory restoration record and any payment/refund side effects required by the business flow. If the review rejects the request, mark the request as rejected and leave the order item unchanged. In both cases, create an immutable cancellation-request snapshot capturing the previous and new request state, reviewer outcome, reason, and timestamps relevant to the decision.

Reject the operation when the order item is not paid or has already been shipped, when the request does not belong to the specified order item, when the request is already closed, or when the caller lacks permission. Ensure no partial state changes occur if any validation fails. Return the updated cancellation request after the transaction commits.

operations.description:
Create a refund request for a single delivered order item.

This operation lets a customer request a refund for one purchased item after delivery, using the order item as the business scope. The refund request is tied to exactly one order item, and the platform stores the customer’s reason together with the current review state so the seller or administrator can process the claim later.

The request is valid only when the target order item is eligible for refund processing and there is no existing active refund request for the same item. The refund workflow is item-level, so other items in the order remain unchanged. When the request is later reviewed, the system records immutable snapshot history for dispute review and audit purposes.

If the order item does not exist, is not refundable, or already has a conflicting refund request, the operation must fail without creating any partial refund record. Authorization must ensure the caller owns the order item context and is allowed to submit the request.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target order item by id and verify it belongs to the authenticated customer. Reject the request if the order item is missing, deleted, not in delivered status, or otherwise ineligible for refund according to business rules. Also reject if a refund request already exists for the same order item, because the schema enforces one refund request per item.

Create the refund request in a transaction using the order item id, authenticated customer id, the item's seller id, the submitted reason, and an initial pending status. Do not allow the client to supply foreign keys or status fields that are derived by the service. If the business layer requires administrator handling, keep the administrator id null at creation.

After insertion, return the created refund request record. If any validation fails, abort without inserting anything. Preserve later lifecycle changes through the refund request snapshot mechanism when the request is reviewed or its state changes.

The returned record is intended for customers viewing their own requests, sellers reviewing requests for their own order items, and administrators handling dispute resolution. Refund requests remain tied to one order item only, and their historical state changes are preserved separately through snapshot records for later review.

Retrieve a paginated list of refund requests for browsing and review.

Refund requests represent item-level refund claims for delivered order items. This endpoint lets customers review their own submitted requests, sellers review requests for items they are responsible for, and administrators browse requests for oversight and dispute handling. Each result reflects the current live state of the request stored in the refund request table, while the immutable snapshot history remains available for later review.

The returned list is intended for operational workflows such as pending request queues, customer history views, seller review screens, and administrative dispute inspection. Results should support filtering by request status, related order item, customer, seller, reviewer, and creation or review time, along with pagination and sorting. When a request has associated reviewer notes or a resolved state, those values should be surfaced consistently with the current record state.

Access control must ensure that customers can only see their own refund requests, sellers can only see requests for their own sold items, and administrators can browse across the platform. If a request no longer exists or has been removed from active visibility, the system should only return it when business rules allow historical access through preserved records or snapshots.

Apply authorization scoping before pagination so each role only receives permitted rows. Return summary rows only, not the full nested snapshot history.

Use stable deterministic ordering, with created_at descending as the default sort for review queues and customer history. If sort fields are provided, validate them against available columns and protect against sorting by unrelated joined data unless explicitly supported. Ensure pagination metadata is consistent even when no rows match. Do not mutate any records. Update a refund request and record the current decision state.

This operation updates an existing refund request for a specific order item. It is used when the responsible reviewer responds to the request, allowing the live refund request record to reflect the new status, review timestamp, reviewer note, and administrator involvement when applicable.

The refund request belongs to one customer, one seller, and one order item. When the request changes, the service must preserve the prior state in the refund request snapshot table so the full review history remains available for dispute resolution and customer support. The operation must also enforce the business rules that only eligible refund requests can transition to a new review state.

If validation fails, the request must not partially update the refund request record. If the refund request does not exist, is not accessible to the current actor, or the requested status transition is invalid, the operation must reject the update without changing stored data.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the refund request by id and lock it for update. Verify the caller is allowed to modify the request according to the refund workflow and ownership rules. Reject missing records and unauthorized access.

Before applying changes, validate the requested transition against the current refund status and the domain rules. Preserve the previous state by inserting a row into mall_platform_refund_request_snapshots containing the before/after status values, the change reason, reviewer role, reviewer note, and creation timestamp. Update the live refund request row in mall_platform_refund_requests in the same transaction so snapshot creation and live-state update remain atomic.

When the status changes to approved or rejected, update reviewed_at and reviewer_note accordingly, and set the administrator reference only when an administrator is the actor taking responsibility for the decision. Keep the response aligned with the current live record after commit. If the request is already in a terminal state or the transition is disallowed, roll back and return a validation error. Never mutate order items or inventory inside this endpoint; those effects belong to downstream business handlers triggered by the approved decision flow.

The product’s review list contributes to its public reputation and rating summary. If the product does not exist, the request must be rejected.

operations.description:
Create a review for a delivered order item.

This operation lets a customer submit feedback for a specific purchased item after the item has reached delivered status. The review is tied to the purchase context of the order item, so eligibility is checked against the referenced order item rather than against the product in general.

The review stores the customer’s star rating and optional written content for the purchased product. The system must reject the request if the item has not been delivered yet, if the customer does not own the order item, or if a review for the same product within the same order already exists. Existing review history is preserved through review snapshots when the review is later edited or deleted.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target order item by id, including its order, customer, product, current status, and existing review relationship. Verify that the authenticated customer owns the order item and that the item status is delivered before allowing creation.

Enforce the one-review-per-product-per-order rule by checking whether a review already exists for the same order item or for the same product within the same order context. If a review exists, reject the request with a conflict-style validation error. Do not allow creation for non-delivered items or for items that belong to another customer.

Insert the new review row with customer_id, order_item_id, product_id, rating, and optional content. Use the order item’s product and customer relationships as the source of truth; do not accept those identifiers from the client body. Return the persisted review entity after creation. If any validation fails, do not create partial data.

Update an existing customer review.

This operation lets a customer edit the rating and written content of a review they previously created for a purchased product. Reviews are part of the product’s public feedback section, so updates affect what customers see on the product detail page, including review ordering and the product’s rating summary.

The system preserves the previous review state by creating a snapshot before applying the update. Only the review owner may perform this action. If the review does not exist, is not owned by the authenticated customer, or cannot be edited because it is no longer active, the request must be rejected with an appropriate error.

operations.specification:
Load the target review by reviewId and verify it exists. Ensure the authenticated customer owns the review; otherwise return a forbidden or not found response consistent with the API’s authorization strategy.

Validate the payload against review rules: rating is required and must be within the allowed star range; text content is optional and should be normalized as provided by the request contract. Before changing any mutable fields, insert a row into mall_platform_review_snapshots capturing the previous review state and the time of change.

Update the mall_platform_reviews row with the new rating and text content. Do not modify ownership, purchase linkage, or other immutable references. After the update, any product rating summary calculations must use the active review set only, so downstream reads should naturally reflect the new active state. If the review is already deleted or otherwise inactive according to domain rules, reject the update.

Delete one of your own product reviews.

This operation allows an authenticated customer to remove a review they previously wrote for a purchased product. The review is no longer treated as active customer feedback after deletion, and it must no longer contribute to the product's average rating or public review listing.

The system preserves the historical review record through snapshot history for dispute resolution and audit purposes. If the customer account is later deleted, preserved reviews continue to be shown as written by a deleted user. Deletion is only permitted for the review owner; attempts to remove another customer's review must be rejected.

If the review does not exist, is already deleted, or does not belong to the authenticated customer, the service must return an appropriate client error. The operation must not remove preserved review snapshots or otherwise break historical order and product records.

operations.specification:
Load the target review by reviewId and verify it exists. Confirm the authenticated customer is the owner of the review; if not, reject with a forbidden or not-found style error according to platform conventions. Also reject deletion when the review is already inactive/deleted.

Before marking the review inactive, create a review snapshot that captures the current review state so the prior text, rating, and ownership context are preserved. Update the active review record so it is no longer counted as active feedback and is excluded from average rating computation and product review listings.

Do not delete snapshot rows. Do not alter preserved historical review identity. If the review participates in any summary cache or denormalized rating field, recalculate the product's average rating using only active, non-deleted reviews. Use a transaction so snapshot creation, review state update, and rating recalculation remain consistent.

Reviews that have been deleted are not part of the active browsing set and must not contribute to ordinary review list results or rating-related display counts. Review snapshots remain available for historical and dispute-related viewing through other operations.

If filtering, pagination, or sorting parameters are invalid, the service must reject the request with a validation error. If the requested page is empty, the response should still succeed with an empty list and consistent paging metadata.

Retrieve the immutable snapshot history for a specific administrator approval request.

This endpoint returns the preserved change history for one administrator approval request so relevant parties can review prior states, review decisions, and status transitions during audits or disputes. Each snapshot belongs to a single parent approval request and records the reason for the snapshot together with the timestamp when it was created.

The history is read-only and reflects the request state over time. Only the owner of the related request and administrators should be able to access these records. If the caller is not a relevant party, the request must be rejected. The endpoint should preserve the chronological ordering of snapshots and support pagination when the history is large.

Return snapshots ordered by createdAt ascending or descending consistently with the platform's list browsing rules, and paginate the result set.
Do not allow mutation operations here; the underlying table is append-only and immutable after creation.
Enforce access control so only the owner of the related approval request and administrators can read the snapshots. If the parent request does not exist, return not found. If the caller is unauthorized, return access denied. Use the snapshot_reason and created_at fields as the primary summary data exposed in the list response.

The response is intended for governance workflows and request monitoring. It should support filtering, sorting, and pagination so reviewers can focus on pending requests, inspect completed decisions, and trace request history when handling duplicate or already-processed submissions. If a request has already reached a final outcome, its stored status remains authoritative and must be reflected consistently in the result set.

The implementation must respect the request lifecycle rules: pending requests are reviewable, completed requests remain immutable in outcome, and duplicate pending requests from the same applicant should not be introduced by this listing operation. If related snapshot records are needed for display badges or audit indicators, fetch them in a read-only manner from mall_platform_administrator_approval_request_snapshots without modifying state.

The response reflects the authoritative request row stored in `mall_platform_administrator_approval_requests`, which preserves the applicant administrator reference, the reviewer administrator reference, the submitted reason, and the current status. Because the table also keeps the review timestamp and optional deletion marker, consumers can distinguish active, reviewed, and cleaned-up records when rendering administrative oversight screens or dispute records.

Update an administrator approval request with a reviewer decision.

This operation is used in the administrator governance workflow to process a single administrator approval request identified by its request ID. The stored record represents an applicant account, the reason submitted by that applicant, the current review status, the reviewer administrator, the rejection reason when applicable, and the review timestamp.

Use this endpoint to approve or reject a pending request. When the request is approved, the applicant becomes a regular administrator. When the request is rejected, the rejection reason must be stored and the request must remain in its final rejected state. Requests that are already approved or rejected must not be modified as if they were still pending.

The request is linked to both the applicant administrator and the reviewer administrator, so implementations must validate that the target request exists, that the reviewer is allowed to process it, and that the transition is consistent with the request's current status. Any invalid transition, missing reason, or attempt to reprocess a final request must be rejected without changing the stored record.

Apply the reviewer decision atomically: update status, set reviewer_administrator_id, set reviewed_at, and set rejection_reason only when rejecting. Keep rejection_reason null when approving unless the schema or business rules explicitly require a value.
If the request is approved, promote the applicant administrator record to regular administrator by ensuring the applicant's grade reflects regular administrator access. If rejected, do not change the applicant's grade.
Do not allow changing the applicant reference or created_at values. Preserve the authoritative stored history of the request.
Return a not-found error when the request id does not exist. Return a validation or conflict error when the request is not pending, when the decision contradicts final-state enforcement, or when required decision data is missing. Persist the update and related administrator grade change in a single transaction.

Administrators can use this endpoint to find pending requests and process the seller approval workflow. Sellers can use the same request list, when permitted by access control, to view their current registration status and understand whether they are pending, approved, or rejected. When a request has been rejected, the stored rejection reason should be included in the summary so the seller can understand the decision.

Results are returned in pages because there may be many review records over time. The service must apply filtering, sorting, and pagination consistently, and it must ignore records that have been marked as deleted. If the requested page is empty, the response should still be a valid paginated result. Access control should prevent unauthorized users from browsing requests they do not own or are not allowed to review.

Use the unique seller_id + created_at constraint only as a data integrity guarantee; do not require it in the API contract.

Enforce validation of status values against pending, approved, and rejected. If the filter requests an unsupported status or an invalid page boundary, return a validation error. Because this is a read-only browsing operation, it must not create snapshots or mutate any seller approval record.

operations.description:
Reorder the images attached to a product.

This operation updates the maintained presentation order for a product’s image set. The first image in the order is treated as the main thumbnail image used in product listings and on the product detail page, so the requested order directly affects how customers see the product across browsing surfaces.

Only the seller who owns the product may perform this action. The product must still exist and remain available for image maintenance. If the requested image sequence is invalid, refers to an unavailable image, or would leave the product without a valid main image position, the request is rejected and the existing image order remains unchanged.

A successful reorder is recorded in the product’s snapshot history so the previous visual presentation can be reconstructed for dispute review and audit purposes.

Apply the reorder atomically so the maintained order changes only if all validations pass. Ensure exactly one first-position image after the update, since the first image is the main thumbnail. Persist the new order on mall_platform_product_images, then create the corresponding product snapshot and product image snapshot history entries to preserve the previous state.

Return the updated product image collection in maintained order. On failure, do not alter the stored order and do not create a snapshot for the failed attempt.

Reorder the images attached to a product.

This operation updates the maintained presentation order for a product’s image set. The first image in the order is treated as the main thumbnail image used in product listings and on the product detail page, so the requested order directly affects how customers see the product across browsing surfaces.

Only the seller who owns the product may perform this action. The product must still exist and remain available for image maintenance. If the requested image sequence is invalid, refers to an unavailable image, or would leave the product without a valid main image position, the request is rejected and the existing image order remains unchanged.

A successful reorder is recorded in the product’s snapshot history so the previous visual presentation can be reconstructed for dispute review and audit purposes.
operations.name: reorderProductImages
operations.specification:
Load the target product by productId and verify the authenticated seller owns it and is allowed to maintain its images. Reject the request if the product does not exist, is unavailable for maintenance, or belongs to another seller.

Validate that the request provides a complete new ordering of existing product image identifiers for that product, with no duplicates and no missing images. Reject any request that references an image not attached to the product or any image that is no longer available.

Apply the reorder atomically so the maintained order changes only if all validations pass. Ensure exactly one first-position image after the update, since the first image is the main thumbnail. Persist the new order on mall_platform_product_images, then create the corresponding product snapshot and product image snapshot history entries to preserve the previous state.

Return the updated product image collection in maintained order. On failure, do not alter the stored order and do not create a snapshot for the failed attempt.

responseBody.description: The updated product image set in its maintained display order after a successful reorder.

parameters.description: Identifier of the product whose images are being reordered.
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: New image ordering for the specified product. The order of identifiers in this body becomes the maintained presentation order, and the first image becomes the main thumbnail image.

operations.description:
Retrieve the current availability state for a product variant.

This endpoint returns the purchasability status of one variant using the variant record and its current stock position. It is intended for product detail pages, cart validation, and seller or administrator review of whether the variant can currently be offered for sale.

The response reflects the variant’s active state together with its inventory-derived availability. A variant may be available, out of stock, or unavailable, and products with no purchasable variants must be treated as unavailable for purchase. If the variant does not exist, is deleted, or belongs to a product that cannot be sold, the request should fail with the appropriate not-found or validation error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the product variant by id and derive availability from the persisted variant record plus current stock calculated from inventory history.
Return a single availability representation for the requested variant only; do not expose unrelated product variants.
Use the mall_platform_product_variants table as the primary source for is_active and product association, and use the inventory history source for current stock calculation. If stock quantity is zero, mark the variant as out of stock. If the variant is inactive, deleted, or otherwise not eligible for purchase, mark it unavailable. If the parent product has no purchasable variants, the variant should not be treated as purchasable even if the row exists.
If the id is invalid or the row is missing, return a not-found error. If inventory history is inconsistent or missing enough records to determine trustable stock, return a business error indicating availability cannot be confirmed. This endpoint is read-only and must not mutate inventory or product state.

responseBody.description: Current availability state for the requested product variant.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product variant (UUID).
parameters.name: productVariantId

operations.description:
Retrieve the immutable snapshot history for a product variant.

This endpoint returns the preserved history of a single product variant so authorized users can review how the variant changed over time, including edits to its SKU code, option values, and price. Variant snapshots are created whenever a seller edits the variant, and they remain available for later audit and dispute review.

The returned history is read-only and represents past states only. It is intended for the variant owner and administrators who need to inspect the variant's change history, including cases where the current product or variant has changed after purchase or other marketplace activity. If the product variant does not exist or the caller is not allowed to view its history, the service should return the appropriate not-found or forbidden error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load snapshot records for the requested product variant using its identifier.
Validate that the product variant exists before querying snapshots. Query the product_variant_snapshots table filtered by product_variant_id, ordered by creation timestamp descending so the newest historical state appears first.

Return an immutable read model that includes the snapshot metadata and the preserved before/after values for each edit. Do not attempt to update, create, or delete snapshot rows. If the product variant is missing, return not found. If the authenticated caller is neither the owning seller nor an administrator, return forbidden. If no snapshots exist, return an empty collection with successful response semantics.

When implementing the response model, ensure it reflects snapshot history rather than the live variant entity. The endpoint should remain safe for deleted variants and deleted parent products as long as the snapshot history still exists, because snapshots are preserved for historical review.

responseBody.description: The immutable history of snapshots for the requested product variant.

parameters.description: The identifier of the product variant whose snapshot history should be returned.
parameters.name: productVariantId

operations.description:
Retrieve the image snapshot history for a product.

This operation returns the preserved history of a product's presentation images so sellers and administrators can review how the product gallery changed over time. Each snapshot captures the image URL, display order, main-thumbnail flag, and the exact time the image state was recorded, which supports audit review and dispute resolution for visual product changes.

The history is scoped to a single product and follows that product through image maintenance actions such as uploads, reordering, and deletions. Only callers with permission to inspect the product may access the snapshot history, and the product must exist; otherwise the request is rejected. The response is ordered chronologically so consumers can reconstruct the image timeline consistently.
operations.name: imageSnapshots
operations.specification:
Load all product image snapshot rows for the requested product id using the product-image snapshot table filtered by mall_platform_product_id. Order results by created_at ascending so the consumer can reconstruct the timeline, or descending only if the platform-wide list convention requires newest-first; keep the ordering consistent with the rest of the product snapshot APIs.

Validate that the product exists and that the caller has permission to view the product or its snapshots. For administrators, allow access to any product; for sellers, allow only the seller who owns the product. If the product does not exist, return a not-found business error. If the product exists but the caller is unauthorized, return an access-denied error.

Return immutable snapshot rows only; do not join live product image rows because deleted or reordered images must still be visible from history. Preserve image_url, image_order, is_main, and changed_at exactly as stored. If the product has no image snapshots, return an empty list rather than an error.

responseBody.description: A chronological list of snapshot records describing the product's image history.

parameters.description: The product identifier whose image snapshot history should be retrieved.
parameters.name: productId

prerequisites.description: A product must be created first because the image snapshot history is scoped to an existing product, and the endpoint should not be called for a non-existent product.

operations.description:
Retrieve the full inventory movement history for a specific product variant.

This operation returns every recorded stock change event for the selected variant, including restocking, manual adjustments, order deductions, and stock restorations caused by cancellations or refunds. The history is used to explain how the variant's current stock position was derived over time and to help sellers review the meaning of each movement.

The history is scoped to the specified product and variant, and only records belonging to that exact variant are returned. If the product or variant does not exist, or if the variant does not belong to the given product, the request must fail with a not-found or scope-mismatch error. The returned records should reflect the inventory history stored in the inventory records table, ordered from oldest to newest or newest to oldest consistently for client display.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the product by productId and verify that the variantId belongs to that product before querying history.

Query mall_platform_inventory_records for rows where mall_platform_product_variant_id equals the resolved variant id. Order the records consistently by created_at, preferably descending for audit display unless the API conventions in this service require ascending timelines.

Return the raw inventory movement history entries with fields from the inventory record schema: id, mall_platform_product_variant_id, quantity_change, reason, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at only if the system exposes archived records. Do not compute current stock here; the client can derive it from the history, and other endpoints should handle stock summaries.

Enforce access control so only authorized parties can view the history: the owning seller for the product, and administrators when platform-wide oversight is permitted. If the variant is not owned by the product, respond with a scope error rather than exposing cross-product data.

Because the inventory record table is effectively append-only, do not provide mutation behavior here. If deleted_at is used in the persisted data model, exclude deleted rows unless the product requirements explicitly allow historical archival visibility.

responseBody.description: Full inventory movement history for the specified product variant.

parameters.description: Identifier of the product that owns the variant.
parameters.name: productId

parameters.description: Identifier of the product variant whose inventory history is being retrieved.
parameters.name: variantId

prerequisites.description: The product must exist first because the inventory history is scoped to a specific product and the variant must belong to that product.
The product variant must already exist under the specified product so the inventory history can be queried for that exact variant.

operations.description:
Create a restocking history entry for a product variant.

This operation records a positive stock movement for a specific product variant so the seller’s inventory trail remains complete and immutable. The new record captures the quantity added, the business reason for the restock, and the time the change was recorded. Current stock is derived from the full history of inventory records, so this operation contributes directly to the variant’s availability state.

The operation is limited to the seller who owns the target product variant. If the referenced variant does not exist, or if the authenticated seller does not own it, the request must be rejected and no inventory record may be created. The variant’s stock history should remain unchanged on failure.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target product variant by productVariantId and verify that it exists and belongs to the authenticated seller. Reject the request with a not-found or forbidden error when the variant is missing or unauthorized.

Validate that the request creates a restock movement only: the quantity change must be positive, the reason must be present, and the record must be written as an immutable inventory history entry. Persist the inventory record in a transaction so the new history row and any downstream stock recalculation remain consistent.

After inserting the record, derive the variant’s current stock from the sum of all inventory records for that variant. If the operation cannot be completed, do not write partial data and do not alter the current stock. Return the created inventory record with its identifier, quantity change, reason, and timestamp.

responseBody.description: The newly created inventory restock record.

parameters.description: The product variant identifier whose inventory history will receive the restock entry.
parameters.name: productVariantId

requestBody.description: Restock details for adding stock to the selected product variant.

operations.description:
Create an inventory adjustment record for a product variant.

This operation records a seller-initiated stock reduction for a single product variant, such as loss, damage, shrinkage, or another manual correction. The record becomes part of the variant's append-only inventory history and contributes to the current stock calculation together with all other inventory movements.

Each adjustment is stored with the signed quantity change, the business reason for the reduction, and the timestamp of the recorded change. The variant is identified by the path parameter, and the adjustment is always applied within that variant's stock history. If the request is invalid or the adjustment cannot be completed, no partial stock change is applied and the existing inventory history remains unchanged.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target product variant by id and verify it exists. Ensure the caller is authorized to modify the variant's inventory and that the variant belongs to a product the seller can manage.

Create a new mall_platform_inventory_records row linked to the variant. The quantity_change must be negative and represent the amount removed from stock for loss, damage, shrinkage, or another manual adjustment. Validate that the adjustment reason is provided and meaningful; reject the request when the reason is empty or unclear. Use the current timestamp for created_at and updated_at.

Recalculate available stock from the full inventory history or update the stock projection in the variant service using the new record. Do not mutate prior inventory history rows. If validation fails or the record cannot be created, abort the operation without changing stock.

Return the created inventory record. Include the persisted reason, quantity change, and timestamps. If the variant does not exist, return a not-found error. If the caller is not allowed to manage the variant, return a forbidden error. If the adjustment would be invalid for business rules, return a validation error.

responseBody.description: The created inventory adjustment history record for the product variant.

parameters.description: Identifier of the product variant whose inventory history will receive the adjustment.
parameters.name: productVariantId

requestBody.description: Details of the manual inventory adjustment to record for the variant.

operations.description:
Retrieve the current shopping cart for the authenticated customer.

This operation returns the customer-owned cart header together with its current line items so the buyer can review selected variants, quantities, item subtotals, and the overall cart total before checkout. The cart reflects the latest purchasable state of each selected product variant, including unavailable or out-of-stock conditions that may affect checkout eligibility.

The cart belongs to exactly one registered customer account and aggregates cart items under that account. Each item represents one selected product variant, so the response should expose the item’s product and variant context, quantity, pricing, and subtotal in a form suitable for cart review and checkout preparation.

Access is restricted to authenticated customer accounts. If the request is made without a valid customer session, the service must reject it. If the cart has not been initialized yet, the service should return the authenticated customer’s current cart representation according to the cart lifecycle rules.
operations.name: get
operations.specification:
Load the current shopping cart for the authenticated customer account.
Query the shopping cart table by the current customer identity from the session context, then load its cart items and the referenced product variant and product data needed for display.
Compute each item subtotal from the current unit price and quantity, and compute the cart total as the sum of all item subtotals.
Include availability indicators for variants that are out of stock or no longer purchasable so the client can block checkout appropriately.
Enforce ownership: never allow access to another customer’s cart.
If no cart row exists yet for the authenticated customer, return the customer’s current cart representation only if the platform auto-creates carts on read; otherwise return the not-found state defined by the cart lifecycle rules.
Reject unauthenticated or non-customer access with the platform’s authorization error handling.

responseBody.description: The authenticated customer’s shopping cart with all current items and pricing totals.

operations.description:
Return the current shopping cart summary for the authenticated customer.

This endpoint provides the pre-checkout view of the customer’s cart, including each selected product variant, its quantity, its subtotal, and the cart-wide total price. It is intended for purchase review before checkout and keeps unavailable items visible so the customer can resolve them before placing an order.

The response reflects the cart pricing rules used across the platform: each line subtotal is derived from the item quantity and current cart price, and the total price is the sum of all visible cart item subtotals. If any item is unavailable or has insufficient stock, that state must be represented in the summary so the customer can make an informed purchase decision.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Fetch the authenticated customer’s current shopping cart summary in a single read query.

Load the customer-owned shopping cart and its cart items, then join the referenced product variant, product, and seller data required to render the summary view. Compute each cart item subtotal from the item quantity and displayed unit price, and compute the cart total as the sum of all item subtotals, including items that remain visible but are unavailable.

Include availability indicators for deleted or out-of-stock variants, and include stock warning state when the variant stock is lower than the selected quantity. Do not allow cross-account access: the result must be scoped strictly to the current authenticated customer. If the customer has no cart, return the empty cart summary shape expected by the UI rather than an error, unless the platform’s auth layer rejects unauthenticated access before this service is reached.

responseBody.description: Current shopping cart summary for the authenticated customer, including cart items, subtotals, availability states, and total price.

operations.description:
Add a selected product variant to the current customer cart.

This operation creates a new cart item for the authenticated customer’s active shopping cart, or merges the quantity into the existing cart line when the same variant is already present. The cart item stores the selected variant, requested quantity, and the current availability state used during checkout validation.

The operation validates that the referenced product variant exists, is active, and can be purchased for the customer’s cart. It also relies on the cart-item uniqueness rule for a single cart and variant pair, so duplicate selections are never stored as separate lines. If the variant is unavailable or the requested quantity cannot be accepted, the request fails without affecting other cart contents.
operations.name: post
operations.specification:
Load the authenticated customer’s active shopping cart, then validate the requested product variant against mall_platform_product_variants and its parent mall_platform_products record. Ensure the variant is active and the product is not deleted or otherwise unavailable for purchase.

If a cart item already exists for the same shopping cart and product variant pair, update that row by increasing the quantity instead of inserting a duplicate. Use the cart-item uniqueness constraint to prevent duplicate lines. Recompute or refresh the cart item availability_state based on the current variant state and requested quantity.

If quantity is invalid or the variant cannot be purchased, reject the request with a validation error and do not mutate the cart. If the customer has no active cart, create or resolve the customer’s cart according to the cart ownership rule, then insert the new line. Return the persisted cart item record after the transaction commits.

responseBody.description: The cart item that was created or updated in the customer’s active cart.

requestBody.description: Variant selection and quantity for a new cart line.

operations.description:
Update the quantity of a cart item in the current customer’s shopping cart.

This operation changes the number of units for a single cart line while keeping the selected product variant unchanged. The cart item belongs to one shopping cart and one product variant, so the update applies only to that specific line and does not affect other items in the cart.

The service must recalculate the cart line subtotal and the cart total after a successful change, and it must reject updates that would violate cart ownership, invalid quantity rules, or current variant availability constraints. If the selected variant is unavailable or the requested quantity exceeds the available stock, the request must fail without partially changing other cart items.
operations.name: putByCartitemid
operations.specification:
Load the cart item by id and verify it belongs to the authenticated customer’s shopping cart. Reject the request if the cart item does not exist, is not owned by the caller, or has been deleted.

Update only the mutable cart-item fields required for quantity adjustment; keep mall_platform_product_variant_id unchanged so the cart line continues to represent the same variant. Validate the requested quantity is a positive integer and within any business-specific cart limits. Check the current product variant state and availability state before persisting the change.

If the quantity is accepted, save the cart item update and then recalculate cart-level totals from the current cart items. Ensure the operation is atomic so a failed validation or persistence error leaves the cart item and all other cart items unchanged. Return appropriate not-found, forbidden, and validation errors for ownership and quantity/availability failures.

responseBody.description: The updated cart item after the quantity change, including the new quantity, recalculated subtotal, and any stock warning state for the selected variant.

parameters.description: Cart item identifier in UUID format.
parameters.name: cartItemId

requestBody.description: Payload for updating the quantity of an existing cart item while keeping the selected variant unchanged.

operations.description:
Remove a selected item from the current customer's shopping cart.

This operation deletes one cart line identified by `cartItemId`, which represents a specific product variant, quantity, and availability state within the authenticated customer's shopping cart. The cart item belongs to a shopping cart, and the cart belongs to a customer account, so the request must be authorized against the current customer’s own cart only.

If the requested cart item does not exist or is no longer present, the system must handle the request safely and leave the remaining cart contents unchanged. After removal, the cart total and item list are recalculated so the client can display the updated shopping cart state consistently.
operations.name: eraseByCartitemid
operations.specification:
Load the cart item by UUID and verify it belongs to the authenticated customer's shopping cart through the shopping cart relation. If the cart item exists, delete only that row and update any cart totals or derived cart summary data used by the read model. If the item is already missing, return success without modifying other cart lines.

Do not touch other cart items in the same shopping cart. Keep the operation idempotent from the user experience perspective so repeated removal requests do not cause errors when the item is already gone. Enforce access control so a customer cannot remove another customer's cart item. Return the current cart representation after deletion so the UI can refresh totals and quantities immediately.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the cart item to remove.
parameters.name: cartItemId

operations.description:
Preview the current shopping cart before placing an order.

This operation returns the authenticated customer’s selected cart items with product names, variant options, per-item subtotals, and the cart total so the purchase can be reviewed before payment is confirmed. It also resolves the chosen shipping address and reports whether every item is still available for checkout.

The preview is tied to the customer’s shopping cart and saved shipping addresses. It does not create an order or change cart contents. If any selected variant is unavailable or insufficiently stocked, the response must include the blocking condition so the customer can correct the cart before proceeding.
operations.name: search
operations.specification:
Read the authenticated customer’s shopping cart and compute a checkout preview without mutating any data.

Load the customer’s active shopping cart and its cart items, then join each item to the related product and product variant records to build the line-item summary. Use product and variant availability checks to determine whether the cart is eligible for checkout, and calculate each line subtotal plus the cart total from the current item quantities and effective item prices.

Resolve the shipping address using the provided shippingAddressId when present; otherwise, use the customer’s default shipping address. If the requested address does not belong to the customer or no usable address exists, return a validation error. Do not persist any checkout state, do not create an order, and do not alter cart quantities, stock, or address data.

Return a checkout preview payload that includes the cart summary, selected shipping address, availability flags, and any warnings needed by the client to block payment when items are deleted, out of stock, or otherwise not purchasable. If the cart is empty, return a business validation error indicating that checkout cannot begin.

responseBody.description: Checkout preview for the authenticated customer’s current cart, including line items, totals, shipping address, and readiness status.

requestBody.description: Checkout preview options for the customer’s current cart, including the shipping address to use for the order review step.

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated customer's paginated order history.

This operation returns a condensed list of orders owned by the current customer account. Each list item exposes the order number, order date, total price, and overall order status so the UI can render an order history page without loading full order details for every row.

The result is sorted by newest order first and supports pagination and filtering for browsing history safely within the customer's own data scope. If the customer has no orders, the response returns an empty page without exposing any other customer's records. Full order details, including items, shipping address, and shipment information, must be retrieved through the order detail endpoint.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_orders for the authenticated customer only. Join or aggregate from mall_platform_order_items as needed to derive the overall order status and summary fields, but never return orders belonging to another customer.

Implement pagination, sorting, and optional search/filter criteria in the request body. Default ordering must be newest first. The summary result must include order number, order date, total price, and derived overall order status only.

Reject requests from unauthenticated users. Do not leak existence of other customers' orders in empty, filtered, or paginated responses. Use the existing order model's preserved values for historical display, and compute overall status consistently with the order history summary rules.

responseBody.description: Paginated order history summaries for the authenticated customer.

requestBody.description: Pagination and optional search/filter criteria for the authenticated customer's order history.

operations.description:
Retrieve the full details of one order from the customer’s order history.

This endpoint lets an authenticated customer open a specific order from the history list and inspect the complete purchase record, including the order number, total price, overall status, shipping destination, purchased items, and shipment information. It is intended for order history review, delivery tracking, and post-purchase support.

The returned order data must remain consistent with the preserved purchase-time records. Item-level details should reflect the associated order item records and their snapshots so the customer can see the product name, variant, quantity, price, and item status exactly as captured when the order was placed. Shipment data should include the items assigned to each shipment and the tracking information stored for that shipment.

Only the owning customer may access this resource. If the order does not exist or does not belong to the current customer, the service should return an authorization-safe not found response. The operation must not expose other customers’ order history, even when the identifier is valid.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Fetch the order by primary order identifier and verify that the authenticated customer owns it before returning any data.
Use a single order query joined with order items, order item snapshots, shipment records, shipment items, and shipping address data as needed to assemble the full detail view. Preserve and return the stored purchase-time snapshots for order items so product name, variant, seller profile, and item pricing remain historically accurate even if source entities changed later.

Apply customer ownership filtering at the database or service layer; do not reveal whether an order exists for another customer. If no matching order is found for the current customer, return a not-found style response. Ensure read-only behavior with no side effects and no history mutation.

Include related shipment information grouped by shipment, with the items included in each shipment and their tracking fields. Use the preserved shipping address attached to the order record. Handle orders with multiple sellers and mixed item statuses by returning all associated items and derived order status as stored or computed from the order record.

responseBody.description: Full order details for one order history entry, including items, shipping address, and shipment information.

parameters.description: Order identifier within the customer’s own order history.
parameters.name: orderId

operations.description:
Retrieve the item-level history for a single order.

This operation returns the purchased line items that belong to one order so the customer can review each product variant, quantity, purchase price, and item status. It is intended to support the order history detail screen where a user opens a past order and inspects the progress of each item individually, especially for mixed-seller orders where different items may move through shipping, delivery, cancellation, or refund states at different times.

The response reflects the preserved order item records for the specified order and should include the order item identity together with the product and variant details needed to understand what was purchased. The API must enforce ownership rules so a customer can only access their own order items, while privileged staff can use the same endpoint according to platform oversight permissions.

If the order does not exist, does not belong to the caller, or cannot be accessed under the caller’s role, the service should return the appropriate not-found or forbidden error. The endpoint should never expose items from another customer’s order, and it should preserve historical data exactly as recorded for the order.

Load the order by orderId and verify the caller has access to the order according to ownership and role rules.
Join order items for the order and project item-level history fields needed for the detail screen, including quantity, item status, price, and preserved product/variant context.
If the implementation uses preserved snapshots for display, include the historical product and variant values captured for the order item rather than current catalog values.
Return items in a stable order suitable for history display, typically matching the order item insertion order or the platform’s item ordering rule.
Reject access when the order belongs to another customer and the caller is not an authorized seller or administrator for that context.
Return not found when the orderId does not resolve to an accessible order record.
Do not mutate any data; this endpoint is read-only.

operations.description:
Retrieve the shipments for a specific order.

This operation returns the delivery packages associated with the given order, including each shipment's seller scope, carrier information, tracking number, tracking URL when available, shipment status, and the order items included in that shipment. It is intended for customer order detail pages and shipment tracking views, where users need to understand which items travel together and how each package is progressing.

Shipments are grouped by seller, and every shipment belongs to exactly one order. A shipment may contain one or more order items, but all of those items must come from the same seller. The response should preserve that relationship so the client can display grouped tracking information and support delivery confirmation per shipment.

If the order does not exist or does not belong to the authenticated customer, the request must be rejected. If the user is not allowed to view the order, the service must return an authorization error. Deleted or inaccessible shipments must not be returned.

operations.specification:
Load the order by id and verify the caller is allowed to view it. For customer access, ensure the order belongs to the authenticated customer; for staff access, apply the platform authorization rules.

Query mall_platform_shipments by mall_platform_order_id, ordered by created_at ascending or descending consistently with the order detail contract. Include the shipment seller relation and the shipmentItems relation, and from shipmentItems load the linked orderItem records so the client can render the included item list. The shipment payload should expose carrier_name, tracking_number, tracking_url, status, shipped_at, delivered_at, and the item membership needed by the UI.

Do not return shipments from other orders. Do not infer shipments from order items alone; use the shipment table and its junction table as the source of truth. If the order has no shipments yet, return an empty collection. If the order id is invalid or not found, return a not-found error.

operations.description:
Approve a pending refund request for a delivered order item.

This operation allows the seller responsible for the order item to approve a customer refund request. The refund request represents the current review state for that item-level post-delivery issue, and the result must be recorded against the existing request record rather than creating a new one.

When approval is recorded, the system must preserve the previous request state in an immutable snapshot before updating the live refund request status. If the request is missing, already decided, or does not belong to the authenticated seller, the operation must fail without changing persisted data.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the refund request by refundRequestId and join or validate the related order item ownership so the authenticated seller matches the seller responsible for the item. Reject the request if it does not exist, if it is not in a pending review state, or if the caller is not the owning seller.

Before updating the live refund request row, insert an immutable refund request snapshot capturing the pre-approval state and the post-approval decision state as required by the refund request snapshot model. Then update the refund request status to approved and persist any reviewer outcome metadata supported by the schema.

After the approval is saved, trigger the downstream refund processing for the associated order item according to platform business rules. Keep the operation transactional so snapshot creation and live-state mutation succeed or fail together. Return the updated refund request as the response body. Do not expose approval for users other than the seller of the target item.

operations.description:
Reject a refund request for a delivered order item.

This operation allows the seller responsible for the order item to review a submitted refund request and reject it with a recorded decision. The refund request is part of the refund workflow for post-delivery issue handling, and the system must preserve the request history by storing a snapshot of the request state around the seller’s response.

When the request is rejected, the associated order item remains delivered and is not marked as refunded. The rejection outcome becomes part of the preserved request history, and the request’s current status is updated accordingly so the customer and seller can see the final decision in later dispute reviews or account history views.

Access is limited to the item’s seller and administrative oversight rules where applicable. If the refund request does not exist, is not in a reviewable state, or the caller is not authorized to respond, the operation must fail without changing the existing request or order item state.

Load the refund request by refundRequestId and verify it exists.
Verify the caller is the seller of the underlying order item and that the request is eligible for review.
Reject the operation if the refund request is already finalized, missing, or not associated with a delivered order item in a reviewable state.

Before changing the request, create a refund request snapshot that preserves the pre-decision state. Then update the refund request status to rejected and persist the reviewer outcome metadata required by the schema. Create or finalize the after-decision snapshot so the history captures both the prior and current state around the seller response.

Do not modify the order item status to refunded. Ensure the order item remains delivered when the rejection is saved.

Return the updated refund request entity after the transaction commits. Use a transaction so the snapshot write and request status update are atomic. If validation or authorization fails, return the appropriate business error and do not write any snapshot or status change.

operations.description:
Submit a new administrator approval request.

This endpoint lets an existing customer or seller formally request elevated administrator access by providing a reason for the request. The system creates a pending administrator approval request record that becomes visible to super administrators for governance review.

The request is tied to the applicant administrator account and preserves the submitted reason, review status, reviewer decision details, and timestamps for the request lifecycle. If the same applicant already has an unresolved request, the submission must be rejected so that only one pending governance request exists at a time.

Invalid account state, duplicate pending submissions, or missing required request details must be rejected without creating a record. Once created, the request remains auditable through its stored status and review metadata.

operations.specification:
Create a new administrator approval request row for the authenticated applicant account.
Validate that the caller is a customer or seller eligible to request administrator access, and reject the operation if the caller already has an unresolved request. Enforce the unique administrator_id constraint and treat it as a duplicate-pending guard in application logic.
Persist administrator_id, reason, status='pending', and timestamps; set reviewer_administrator_id, rejection_reason, and reviewed_at to null on creation. If the persistence layer raises a unique constraint violation, translate it to the duplicate-pending business error.
Do not update any administrator role or grade here; this endpoint only records the request. Return the created request entity after insert.

operations.description:
Submit a final decision for an administrator approval request.

This operation lets a super administrator review a pending administrator access request and record the outcome as approved or rejected. The request is identified by its administrator approval request ID, and the decision updates the authoritative request record that stores the applicant, the original reason, the reviewer, the review timestamp, and the final status.

When the decision is approved, the requesting account becomes eligible for administrator access according to the platform's governance rules. When the decision is rejected, the request retains the rejection reason and remains available as part of the immutable approval history. If the request has already been decided, the service should reject the operation to prevent duplicate reviews or inconsistent governance records.

operations.specification:
Load the target administrator approval request by id and verify it exists and is not already finalized in a conflicting way. Require the caller to be a super administrator; regular administrators must be rejected. Validate the decision payload as either approve or reject, and require a rejection reason when the outcome is rejected.

On success, update the administrator approval request row with the reviewer administrator id, reviewed_at timestamp, status, and rejection_reason when applicable. If approved, set the status to approved and clear any rejection reason. If rejected, set the status to rejected and persist the rejection reason. Create a new administrator approval request snapshot row capturing the reason for the state change and the current decision outcome so the review history remains traceable. Use a transaction so the request update and snapshot insert are atomic.

If the request does not exist, return a not-found error. If the request is already reviewed, return a conflict or validation error depending on the platform convention. If the caller lacks super administrator privileges, return forbidden. Preserve the original request reason and do not mutate unrelated fields such as created_at or administrator_id.

responseBody.description: The updated administrator approval request after the decision has been recorded.

operations.description:
Retrieve the current seller approval status.

This operation returns the seller account’s registration review state so the caller can determine whether the seller is pending review, approved to sell, or rejected. When the status is rejected, the response also includes the stored rejection reason so the seller can understand why the request was not approved.

The approval status comes directly from the seller account record and represents the authoritative review result for seller onboarding. If the seller account cannot be resolved in the current access context, the service should return an appropriate not-found or unavailable error instead of inventing a status.

Load the current seller account approval state from mall_platform_seller_accounts. Return approval_status and rejection_reason from the seller account row, and do not expose password_hash or any internal lifecycle timestamps in the response mapping unless the response schema explicitly includes them. Treat approval_status as the authoritative value and preserve its exact domain values: pending, approved, rejected.

If the seller account is missing, banned, suspended, or deleted in a way that makes the current status unavailable for the caller’s business context, return the appropriate domain error according to the auth and account-access rules. Do not modify any data. No joins are needed for this operation because the seller approval state is stored directly on the seller account record. Ensure the endpoint remains read-only and fast, with a single indexed lookup by the authenticated seller context or resolved seller identity.

operations.description:
Approve a seller registration request.

This operation lets an administrator complete the review of a seller onboarding request and mark it as approved so the seller account may proceed to selling activity. The request is tied to a single seller account and represents the live approval lifecycle record for that seller's registration attempt.

When the request is approved, the system records the review time and updates the request status accordingly. The request remains part of the seller's approval history and can be used later for administrative inspection or dispute review. If the request is not in a state that can be approved, the operation must fail without changing the stored record.

Persist the change atomically in a single transaction. If authorization fails, return a forbidden error. If the request is missing, return not found. If the request is already finalized, return a conflict or validation error according to the service error conventions. Return the updated seller approval request after the write succeeds.

The request belongs to the seller approval workflow and includes the applicant seller account reference, the submitted reason, the current review status, and the reviewer decision details that are stored in the `mall_platform_seller_approval_requests` table.

A rejection must include a clear rejection reason so the seller can understand why the request was denied. The seller approval request remains part of the approval history and may later be superseded by a new registration request from the same seller, while the rejection result is preserved for review and audit purposes. Only administrator accounts are allowed to perform this action.

If the request does not exist, is not pending, or the caller is not an administrator, the system must reject the operation and leave the request unchanged. Validation must also ensure that the rejection reason is provided and is meaningful before the rejection is persisted.
