text: The API interface phase is already up to date, so the next correct step is generating the E2E test functions. I’ll run the test agent using the full testing-related requirements from your platform spec.

instruction:
Make the e2e test functions for an e-commerce shopping mall platform with the following requirements.

# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform

I want to create an e-commerce shopping mall platform.

## Customer Account

- This platform requires registration to use any features (no guest browsing)
- Customers sign up with email and password
- Customers log in with email and password
- Customers can change their password
- Customers can delete their account
- When a customer deletes their account:
  - Their profile information is deleted
  - Their orders and order history are preserved (for seller records and legal purposes)
  - Their reviews are preserved but shown as "deleted user"

## Customer Profile

- Each customer has a profile with: display name and phone number
- Customers can edit their display name and phone number

## Address Management

- Customers can add multiple shipping addresses
- Each address has: recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state/province, postal code, country
- Customers can edit their addresses
- Customers can delete their addresses
- Customers can set one address as the default shipping address

## Seller Account

- Sellers sign up with email and password
- Sellers log in with email and password
- Sellers can change their password
- Seller accounts require administrator approval before they can sell
- Sellers can view their approval status (pending, approved, rejected)
- If rejected, sellers can view the rejection reason
- Rejected sellers can submit a new registration request
- Sellers can delete their account only if:
  - They have no pending orders (paid or shipped status)
  - They have no pending cancellation or refund requests
- When a seller deletes their account:
  - Their products are deleted from listings
  - Order history and snapshots are preserved
  - Their shop name in past orders is preserved

## Seller Profile

- Each seller has a profile with: shop name, shop description, and logo image
- Sellers can edit their shop name, description, and logo
- Every edit creates a snapshot
- Customers can view seller profiles

## Categories

- Products are organized into categories
- Categories can have subcategories (one level of nesting only)
- Each category has: name and description
- Categories are created and managed by administrators only
- Customers can browse the list of all categories
- Customers can view products within a category

## Snapshot Principle

- This is a platform where money is exchanged, so all data modifications must be recorded
- Whenever editable data is modified, a snapshot is created to preserve the previous state
- Snapshots record: when the change was made, what was changed, and the values before and after
- Snapshots are immutable and cannot be deleted
- Snapshots can be viewed by relevant parties (owners, administrators) for dispute resolution

**Product Snapshot Structure**
- When a product is edited, a product snapshot is created
- The product snapshot includes all product fields (name, description, category, base price, images)
- The product snapshot also includes snapshots of all variants at that moment (product-snapshot → product-snapshot-SKU)
- This preserves the complete state of a product and its variants at any point in time

**Snapshot applies to:**
- Products (all fields including images)
- Product variants (SKU code, option values, price)
- Seller profiles (shop name, description, logo)
- Order items (product, variant, and seller profile at time of purchase)
- Reviews (rating, text content)
- Cancellation requests (reason, status changes)
- Refund requests (reason, status changes)

## Products

- Sellers can create products
- Every product has:
  - Name (required)
  - Description (required)
  - Category (required, can select a subcategory)
  - Base price (required)
- Products belong to the seller who created them
- Sellers can edit their own products
- Every edit creates a snapshot
- Sellers can delete their own products only if:
  - There are no pending order items (paid or shipped status) for any variant of the product
  - There are no pending cancellation or refund requests for any variant of the product
- Deleting a product also deletes all its variants and inventory records
- Deleted products no longer appear in search or category listings
- Sellers can view snapshots of their own products
- Administrators can view snapshots of any product
- Snapshots are preserved even after product deletion

## Product Images

- Sellers can upload multiple images for each product
- Images can be reordered (first image is the main/thumbnail image)
- Sellers can delete images from their products
- Image changes are included in product snapshots

## Product Variants (SKU)

- A product can have multiple variants
- Each variant represents a specific combination of options (e.g., "Red / Large", "Blue / Small")
- Each variant has:
  - SKU code (unique identifier, required)
  - Option values (e.g., color: "Red", size: "Large")
  - Price (can override the base price, optional)
  - Stock quantity (required, starts at 0)
- Sellers can add variants to their products
- Sellers can edit variants (SKU code, option values, price)
- Every variant edit creates a snapshot
- Sellers can delete variants only if:
  - There are no pending order items (paid or shipped status) for that variant
  - There are no pending cancellation or refund requests for that variant
- A product must have at least one variant to be purchasable
- Products with no variants are visible in search but shown as "unavailable"

## Inventory Management

- Each variant has its own stock quantity
- Stock quantity is managed through inventory history records (not snapshots)
- Each inventory record contains: quantity change (positive for restocking, negative for orders/adjustments), reason, and timestamp
- Current stock is calculated by summing all inventory records
- Sellers can add inventory (restock) with a quantity and reason
- Sellers can subtract inventory (adjustment/loss) with a quantity and reason
- Order placement automatically creates a negative inventory record
- Order cancellation/refund automatically creates a positive inventory record
- Sellers can view the full inventory history of each variant
- When stock reaches 0, the variant is shown as "out of stock"
- Out of stock variants cannot be added to cart

## Product Search

- Customers can search products by name
- Search results show products from all sellers
- Search results are paginated
- Customers can filter search results by:
  - Category
  - Price range (minimum and maximum)
  - In-stock only
- Customers can sort search results by:
  - Newest first
  - Price (low to high)
  - Price (high to low)

## Product Listing

- When viewing a list of products (search results, category page), each product shows:
  - Main image (thumbnail)
  - Name
  - Base price (or price range if variants have different prices)
  - Seller shop name
  - Average rating (if reviews exist)

## Product Detail Page

- Customers can view a single product's full details
- The page shows:
  - All images
  - Name and description
  - Category
  - Seller shop name (links to seller profile)
  - All available variants with prices and stock status
  - Average rating and total review count
  - All reviews

## Wishlist

- Customers can add products to their wishlist
- Customers can view their wishlist
- The wishlist is paginated
- Wishlist shows products (not specific variants)
- Customers can remove products from their wishlist
- If a product is deleted by the seller, it is automatically removed from all wishlists

## Shopping Cart

- Customers can add variants to their cart (must select a specific variant, not just a product)
- When adding to cart, customers specify the quantity
- If the same variant is already in the cart, the quantities are combined (not added as a separate line)
- Customers can view their cart
- Cart shows each item with: product name, variant options, price, quantity, and subtotal
- Customers can change the quantity of items in their cart
- Customers can remove items from their cart
- Cart shows the total price of all items
- If a variant's stock is less than the cart quantity, a warning is shown
- If a variant is deleted or out of stock, it is marked as unavailable in the cart

## Checkout

- Customers can proceed to checkout from their cart
- Unavailable items cannot be checked out
- Customers must select a shipping address (or use default)
- Customers can review the order summary before placing the order:
  - List of items with prices
  - Shipping address
  - Total price
- Once an order is placed, the shipping address cannot be changed

## Payment

- After reviewing, customers confirm and place the order
- Payment is processed (assume external payment gateway integration)
- Payment can succeed or fail
- If payment fails, the order is not created and customers can retry
- If payment succeeds, the order is created

## Order Creation

- When an order is placed successfully:
  - Stock quantities are decreased for each purchased variant
  - Items are removed from the customer's cart
  - An order record is created
  - Each purchased variant becomes an order item with status "paid"
  - A snapshot of each purchased product and variant is saved with the order item (preserves product name, description, variant options, and price at the time of purchase)
  - A snapshot of each seller's profile is saved with the order item (preserves shop name and logo at the time of purchase)

## Order Structure

- An order contains one or more order items
- Each order item represents a purchased product variant with a quantity
- If a customer buys 3 of the same variant, it becomes one order item with quantity 3
- Order items can be from different sellers
- Each order item has its own status
- Each order item can be individually cancelled or refunded
- Order items are grouped into shipments when shipped (see Shipping and Tracking)

## Order History

- Customers can view a list of all their orders
- The list is paginated and sorted by newest first
- Each order in the list shows: order number, date, total price, and overall order status
- Customers can view the full details of an order:
  - List of items with: product name, variant, quantity, price, and item status
  - Shipping address
  - List of shipments with tracking information (each shipment shows which items are included)

## Order Status

**Order Item Status**
- Each item in an order has its own status
- Item statuses:
  - Paid: payment completed, waiting for seller to ship
  - Shipped: seller has shipped the item
  - Delivered: item has been delivered
  - Cancelled: item was cancelled
  - Refunded: item was refunded

**Order Status**
- The overall order status is derived from its items
- If all items are paid → order is "paid"
- If any item is shipped (and none delivered yet) → order is "shipped"
- If all items are delivered → order is "delivered"
- If all items are cancelled → order is "cancelled"
- If all items are refunded → order is "refunded"
- Mixed states (e.g., some delivered, some refunded) → order is "partially completed"

## Shipping and Tracking

**Shipment Concept**
- A shipment is a package sent by a seller
- A shipment can contain one or more order items from the same seller
- Different sellers always ship separately (different shipments)
- A seller can choose to ship items individually or bundle multiple items into one shipment

**Shipping Process**
- Sellers can view order items for their products that need shipping
- When shipping, sellers select one or more of their items to include in a shipment
- Sellers enter tracking information for the shipment (carrier name, tracking number)
- All items in the same shipment share the same tracking information
- When a shipment is created, all items in it change to status "shipped"

**Delivery Confirmation**
- Customers can view tracking information for each shipment
- Customers confirm delivery per shipment (not per item)
- When the customer confirms delivery, all items in that shipment change to status "delivered"
- If the customer does not confirm, items automatically change to "delivered" after 14 days from shipping

## Order Cancellation

- Cancellation is handled per order item, not per entire order
- Customers can request cancellation for individual items with status "paid" (not yet shipped)
- Cancellation requests include a reason (text)
- The seller of that item can approve or reject the cancellation request
- When a seller responds, a snapshot of the request state is created
- If approved, that item is cancelled and refund is processed for that item only
- Cancelled items restore their stock quantities (via inventory record)
- The remaining items in the order continue processing normally
- If all items in an order are cancelled, the entire order status becomes "cancelled"

## Refund Requests

- Refund is handled per order item, not per entire order
- Customers can request a refund for individual items with status "delivered"
- Refund requests include a reason (text)
- Refund can be requested within 7 days of that item being delivered
- The seller of that item can approve or reject the refund request
- When a seller responds, a snapshot of the request state is created
- If approved, that item is refunded
- Refunded items restore their stock quantities (via inventory record)
- The remaining items in the order are unaffected
- If all items in an order are refunded, the entire order status becomes "refunded"

## Reviews and Ratings

- Customers can write a review for products they have purchased
- A review can only be written after that item's status is "delivered"
- Customers can write one review per product per order
- Each review has:
  - Rating (1 to 5 stars, required)
  - Text content (optional)
- Reviews are displayed on the product detail page
- Reviews are sorted by newest first
- Customers can edit their own reviews
- Every review edit creates a snapshot
- Customers can delete their own reviews (but snapshots are preserved)
- Product's average rating is calculated from all non-deleted reviews

## Seller Dashboard

- Sellers can view a summary of their shop:
  - Total number of products
  - Total number of order items (for their products)
  - Number of pending cancellation requests
  - Number of pending refund requests
- Sellers can view a list of all order items for their products
- Sellers can filter order items by status

## Administrator System

**Becoming an Administrator**
- Any user (customer or seller) can submit a request to become an administrator
- The request includes a reason (text)
- Super administrators can view the list of pending requests
- Super administrators can approve or reject requests
- When approved, the user becomes a regular administrator

**Administrator Grades**
- There are two grades: regular administrator and super administrator
- Super administrators can promote regular administrators to super administrator
- Super administrators can demote other super administrators to regular administrator
- Super administrators cannot demote themselves

**Seller Management**
- Administrators can view the list of pending seller approvals
- Administrators can approve or reject seller registrations
- When rejecting, administrators must provide a reason
- Rejected sellers can submit a new registration request
- Administrators can suspend seller accounts
- When a seller is suspended:
  - Their products are hidden from search and category listings
  - Their products cannot be purchased
  - They can still process existing orders (ship items, respond to cancellation/refund requests)
  - They cannot create new products or edit existing products
- Administrators can unsuspend seller accounts (products become visible again)

**Category Management**
- Administrators can create categories and subcategories
- Administrators can edit category names and descriptions
- Administrators can delete categories (products in deleted categories become uncategorized)

**Product Oversight**
- Administrators can view all products on the platform
- Administrators can view snapshots of any product
- Administrators can delete any product (for policy violations)

**Order Oversight**
- Administrators can view all orders on the platform
- Administrators can force-cancel individual items or entire orders (refunds the customer, restores stock)
- Administrators can force-refund individual items or entire orders

**User Management**
- Administrators can view all customer accounts
- Administrators can ban customers (banned customers cannot log in)
- Administrators can unban customers
- Administrators can view all seller accounts
- Administrators can ban sellers (banned sellers cannot log in, existing orders remain)

The test should cover a seller in approved or pending status and assert that the response includes the seller identity, email, account status, rejection reason when present, lifecycle timestamps, and public profile fields such as shop name, description, and logo reference. Confirm that sensitive authentication data is not exposed. Also validate that the API preserves the seller account status exactly as stored, so rejected sellers return their rejection reason verbatim and non-rejected sellers return a null rejection reason.

functions.name: test_api_seller_account_retrieve_with_profile

scenario.draft: Verify administrator access control for seller account retrieval. An authenticated administrator should be able to read any seller account visible to platform governance, while a non-administrator actor must not be able to use this endpoint. The scenario should ensure the operation is treated as privileged administrative inspection rather than seller self-service or customer browsing. Confirm the endpoint only succeeds when called with administrator credentials and that the returned data reflects the seller account plus public shop profile, not private account internals.

functions.name: test_api_seller_account_administrator_only_access

The response should indicate that the seller record is inaccessible because it does not exist, and no partial seller profile data should be returned. dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because the lookup endpoint is restricted to administrator users.

functions.name: test_api_seller_account_not_found_by_id

scenario.draft: Test the administrator account listing for governance workflows. Cover the primary success path where an authenticated administrator retrieves the paginated list and sees only summary fields, with stable default ordering by newest accounts when no sort is provided. Verify that the response includes pagination metadata and does not expose credential data or internal relations. Add a filtering scenario that narrows the list by administrator grade, status, and email search term, then confirms that every returned row matches the requested criteria and pagination remains consistent. Include an edge case where the filters match no records, and the API returns an empty page with correct pagination metadata instead of an error. Because this endpoint is restricted to administrators, also validate that the operation is only exercised after administrator authentication and that the scenario setup uses administrator join/login as appropriate for the test environment.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator before accessing the privileged governance list.

functions.name: test_api_administrator_account_listing

scenario.draft: As an authenticated administrator, verify that the administrator list endpoint returns paginated summary results for governance browsing. Confirm that the response supports stable page navigation across multiple pages, does not duplicate or skip records between pages when using consistent sort controls, and returns pagination metadata that matches the requested page progression. Also confirm that the data exposed remains summary-level only rather than full account detail. This scenario should focus on business browsing behavior for administrative oversight and should use a valid administrator session established before calling the endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator before accessing the privileged administrator list endpoint.

functions.name: test_api_administrator_account_pagination_sorting

scenario.draft: Test that the administrator list is protected from unauthorized access by non-administrator actors. Attempt to reach the governance list without the required administrator context and confirm the platform denies access rather than exposing any administrator account summaries. This scenario validates the privilege boundary for a sensitive moderation endpoint and ensures the operation is available only to the administrator role. The expectation is an authorization failure, not an input validation failure, and the response should not reveal whether specific administrator accounts exist.

The scenario should also ensure the call does not change any account state, hierarchy, or audit-visible fields when the target record is absent. This protects governance screens from showing stale or fabricated administrator identities.

Assert that the response is a page structure with pagination metadata and a data array, that each session item includes the session id, customer summary, IP, href, referrer, createdAt, and expiredAt, and that no sensitive session secrets are exposed. Also verify that the returned sessions belong only to the authenticated customer and that list ordering is deterministic when the same filter and page criteria are repeated.

Query the endpoint with filters such as created-at range, expiration range, IP, href, or referrer, and confirm that only matching sessions are returned. Validate that pagination metadata reflects the filtered result set correctly, that page boundaries are respected, and that an empty page is returned when no sessions match the chosen criteria rather than an error. This scenario should focus on business search behavior and deterministic paging rather than input-validation errors.

The expected behavior is that results remain restricted to the caller's own sessions only, or the request is rejected according to authorization rules; in either case, the response must not leak the other customer's session summaries. Also confirm that a normal request without cross-account filtering still returns only the caller's sessions and preserves the customer summary relationship inside each session row.

scenario.draft: Test the customer password reset flow where a registered customer uses a valid recovery token to set a new password. Verify that the reset succeeds only when the token is active and associated with an eligible account, and that the account can then authenticate with the new password while the old password no longer works. Also verify that the recovery token is consumed so the same token cannot be reused for another reset attempt. Keep the scenario focused on the business outcome of credential recovery rather than request-shape validation.

functions.name: test_api_customer_password_reset_success

scenario.draft: Test the customer password reset flow using a valid recovery token, then verify that the same token cannot be reused after a successful reset and cannot be used after expiry. First create a customer account, then create a password reset request to obtain a usable recovery token, perform one successful password reset with that token, and confirm the customer can authenticate with the new password. After that, attempt to use the same consumed token again and also verify that an expired token is rejected, ensuring no additional credential change occurs and the account remains accessible only with the most recently set password.

scenario.draft: Test that a password reset request with a token that does not correspond to an active recovery record leaves the account unchanged. Focus on the business guarantee that an unknown, invalid, or otherwise unmatched recovery token cannot be used to alter credentials, and that the customer must still sign in with the previously valid password afterward. This scenario should confirm that no accidental password replacement occurs when the recovery reference is not valid.

Also confirm the response preserves the paginated reset-record wrapper and that the associated reset record still reflects the correct linked administrator context and lifecycle timestamps after the operation.

Immediately retry the same reset token with another password and confirm the system rejects the second attempt as an already-consumed recovery token, leaving the account password unchanged from the first successful reset. The focus is on the business rule that password recovery is single-use and that token invalidation happens atomically with the credential update.

This scenario validates the business rule that only active recovery tokens can complete password recovery and that failed recovery attempts do not modify credentials.

In a second assertion path, request a record that has been soft-deleted or is otherwise inaccessible and confirm the service treats it as not found/inaccessible rather than exposing stale recovery data.

dependencies.purpose:
Multi-actor authentication setup:
This join operation (post /mallPlatform/auth/administrator/join) is required to establish a 'administrator' actor user account in the system.
This scenario involves multiple authorization actors, requiring separate user accounts for each actor to properly test cross-actor interactions and authorization boundaries.
The join operation creates the foundational user identity that will be used throughout the test scenario for 'administrator' specific operations.
This join operation is required for the 'administrator' actor authentication.

Actor switching authentication:

functions.name: test_api_category_create_subcategory_admin_only_access

scenario.draft: Verify that an administrator can create exactly one direct subcategory under a valid parent category, and that the platform preserves the one-level category hierarchy rule. The test should create a subcategory under an active parent category, confirm the new category is accepted as a direct child, and then validate that the taxonomy does not allow deeper nesting beyond one parent-child level. Also confirm that a deleted or otherwise inactive parent category is not eligible for new subcategories as part of the business workflow, rather than treating this as a framework validation case.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because only administrators can manage category structure.

functions.name: test_api_category_create_subcategory_hierarchy_restriction

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated administrator can update a category’s name and description while keeping the category record and its browsing identity intact. The test should create or identify an existing top-level category, then submit a valid update that changes only editable fields. Confirm the response reflects the updated category and that the category remains visible to customer category browsing with the same identifier. Also verify that any products already assigned to the category still reference the same category record after the update. This scenario validates the primary successful edit workflow and that a category update does not break existing product/category relationships.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because category management is administrator-only.

functions.name: test_api_category_update_name_description

scenario.draft: Verify that an administrator can move a category to become a direct subcategory of an existing top-level category, and that the one-level hierarchy rule is preserved. Prepare two categories where the intended parent is a top-level category with no parent of its own. Update the child category with a valid parentCategoryId and confirm the updated response shows the new parent relationship. Then verify the original category tree remains shallow: the chosen parent has the updated category as a direct child, and no deeper nesting is introduced. This scenario validates the supported hierarchy reassignment workflow.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because category hierarchy changes are restricted to administrators.

functions.name: test_api_category_update_parent_assignment

scenario.draft: Verify that category updates are rejected when the requested hierarchy change would violate the one-level nesting rule. Use an administrator-authenticated context and attempt to update a category so that it becomes a child of a category that is itself already a subcategory, or otherwise create circular/deeper nesting. Confirm the system does not apply any partial change and that the existing category structure remains unchanged after the failed request. This scenario covers the critical structural protection for category management and ensures invalid hierarchy updates do not corrupt the taxonomy.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because only administrators can attempt category updates.

functions.name: test_api_category_update_reject_deep_nesting

scenario.draft: Test that an authenticated administrator can delete an existing category that has no direct subcategories, and that the category is removed from the admin-managed taxonomy while products previously assigned to it remain available and become uncategorized. Validate that category browsing no longer shows the deleted category, but related products still appear in search/category browsing without exposing the deleted category. Also confirm that deletion does not affect unrelated categories, products, variants, inventory, or snapshots.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because category deletion is admin-only.

functions.name: test_api_category_delete_leaf_category

scenario.draft: Test the business rule for deleting a category that still has direct subcategories. Verify the system handles the one-level hierarchy safely by rejecting the deletion or otherwise applying the platform's defined category-deletion behavior consistently, without leaving the category tree in an invalid state. Confirm that no partial changes are applied: the parent category remains in place if deletion is not allowed, and subcategories and product classification remain consistent after the request.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because category deletion is admin-only.

functions.name: test_api_category_delete_with_subcategories

scenario.draft: Test the customer-facing product catalog browse flow with a valid authenticated customer. Verify the endpoint returns a paginated list of active products across sellers, includes product summary data needed for browse cards, and respects the default browse behavior when no filters are supplied. Validate that each result exposes the main product identity and listing context, including seller shop information and category context, and that deleted or otherwise unavailable products are excluded from the page. Confirm pagination metadata is consistent with the returned data and that the response is read-only.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because the operation requires customer authorization before browsing products.

functions.name: test_api_customer_products_browse_catalog

scenario.draft: Test filtered browsing for a customer using keyword search, category filtering, in-stock-only filtering, and price range criteria together. Verify the returned products match the search term against product name and description, are limited to the selected category, and honor the requested price bounds and stock-only restriction. Confirm the response remains correctly paginated and sorted using one of the supported sort modes, and that products with no matching variants or out-of-stock variants are excluded when the stock-only flag is enabled. Also confirm that an empty match set returns an empty page rather than an error.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because catalog search and filtering require customer access.

functions.name: test_api_customer_products_filtered_search

scenario.draft: Test catalog browsing edge cases for price and category handling. Verify that the endpoint rejects unsupported sorting values and invalid category references according to the browsing rules, while still allowing normal requests with a valid sort option such as newest, priceAsc, or priceDesc. Confirm the price filtering behavior produces a stable page of results and that boundary values for minimum and maximum price are honored inclusively. This scenario should emphasize business behavior around browse filters, not transport or framework-level validation.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because the product listing endpoint is customer-scoped.

functions.name: test_api_customer_products_browse_filter_boundaries

scenario.draft: Test that a seller can browse the active marketplace product catalog with the default listing behavior and that the response is a properly paginated product summary page. Verify the returned page includes products from the active catalog only, with seller shop name context, category context when present, and list-ready pricing/display data. Confirm pagination metadata is consistent with the returned items and that results are stable enough for browse use. Also verify that soft-deleted/unavailable products do not appear in the active browse list. This scenario should validate the primary seller-facing browse experience without relying on any filters.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller because this catalog browsing endpoint requires seller authorization.

functions.name: test_api_product_catalog_browse_active_listing

scenario.draft: Test seller-side product browsing and filtering on the marketplace catalog list. Authenticate as a seller, then request the paginated product list with combinations of keyword search, category filtering, price range filtering, and in-stock-only filtering. Verify that the response narrows results according to all applied filters, remains paginated, and includes the expected list fields such as product summary information, seller shop context, thumbnail/main image, and pricing summary. Confirm that products with no available stock are excluded when in-stock-only is enabled, while matching in-stock products remain visible.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller because this browsing endpoint is seller-scoped.

functions.name: test_api_product_catalog_filtered_search

scenario.draft: Test boundary and empty-result behavior for the product browse endpoint. Query with a legitimate filter combination that is expected to return no products, and confirm the API returns an empty page rather than an error. Also verify that the paging metadata remains valid for the empty result set and that the response shape is still the normal paginated product summary structure. In the same scenario, confirm that unsupported browsing combinations are not accepted by business rules by using the endpoint only through valid inputs already known to be supported, while focusing the assertion on graceful empty browsing behavior rather than input validation errors. This protects the catalog UI from breaking when no products match a seller’s browse conditions.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller because the endpoint requires seller access before browsing the catalog.

functions.name: test_api_product_catalog_empty_result_page

scenario.draft: Test that an administrator can browse the marketplace product catalog with pagination and the key filters/sort options supported by the endpoint. Verify the response returns a page of product summaries with seller shop context, category context, base price, and pagination metadata. Cover a primary success case using a valid category filter, keyword search, in-stock-only filtering, and a supported sort order such as newest or priceAsc. Confirm deleted or otherwise unavailable products are excluded from the result set. Also verify that an empty matching result returns an empty page rather than an error. Because this endpoint is admin-scoped, ensure the request succeeds only when executed with administrator access.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator before calling the admin-only product browse endpoint.
Create a category that can be used as a valid category filter in the product browse request.

functions.name: test_api_product_catalog_admin_browse

scenario.draft: Authenticate as an administrator, then verify the product browsing endpoint returns a paginated catalog list that respects price-range filtering, page boundaries, and product visibility rules. Seed representative products across multiple price points and lifecycle states so the response can be checked for: products inside the requested min/max range, products outside the range being excluded, products with no active availability still appearing according to browse rules, and deleted products being omitted. Confirm pagination metadata is correct across the first page and a page request beyond the available results, which should return an empty page with valid pagination data. Also verify the response remains a list of product summaries appropriate for catalog browsing.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator before using the administrator product browsing endpoint.

functions.name: test_api_product_catalog_price_range_pagination

scenario.draft: Test product browsing when the request references category and sort inputs that the service must validate against live marketplace data. Confirm that a valid existing category can be used to narrow the result set, and that the listed products still include seller summary, category summary, base price, and timestamps. Also validate that unsupported sort values are not used in normal flows and that the supported sort modes reorder products deterministically. If the catalog contains products from multiple sellers, verify that each summary carries the correct seller account information and that the endpoint remains read-only with no side effects on inventory, wishlist, or cart data.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator before calling the browse endpoint.
Create a category so the browse request can filter by an existing category reference.

functions.name: test_api_product_catalog_category_filtered_sorting

scenario.draft: Verify the customer can open a product detail page and receive the full live product view for an available product. The response should include the product’s seller summary, optional category, name, description, base price, ordered images, current variants, and review-related presentation data. Confirm the returned relations reflect the current state rather than snapshot data, and that the product detail is stable enough for customer browsing. Also validate that a customer can retrieve a product that belongs to a seller with an approved, visible storefront, and that the response reflects deterministic ordering for images and variants.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer before accessing shopper-facing product detail.

functions.name: test_api_product_detail_view

scenario.draft: Verify the product detail endpoint respects marketplace visibility rules when the product is no longer browsable. The scenario should cover a product that has been deleted or otherwise made unavailable under platform rules, or belongs to a seller that is not visible for browsing, and the request should return a not-found or unavailable-style response. This ensures customers cannot access inactive catalog items through direct lookup even if they know the identifier.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer before attempting to load a product through the shopper endpoint.

functions.name: test_api_product_detail_unavailable_product

scenario.draft: Verify that a customer can view a product that currently has no variants and that the product is still displayed as an available catalog item for browsing but marked as unavailable for purchase. Confirm the product detail view shows the seller and category context and that the business state reflects no purchasable variant options, so the product cannot be added to checkout while still remaining visible on the marketplace.

Validate that the detail view reflects deterministic ordering for related collections and that the returned seller and category references match the product's current ownership and classification. functions.name: test_api_product_detail_retrieve_full_view

This scenario should ensure deleted products and ineligible seller states are not treated as visible marketplace detail pages.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller because the operation requires seller authorization.

functions.name: test_api_product_detail_unavailable_visibility

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller because the operation requires seller authorization.

functions.name: test_api_product_detail_without_variants

scenario.draft: Test that an authenticated administrator can retrieve a live product’s full detail view for an active product they are allowed to inspect. dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because the endpoint requires administrator access.

functions.name: test_api_product_administrator_retrieve_detail

scenario.draft: Test that the administrator can retrieve a product that is categorized under a subcategory and that the detail response preserves the linked category context correctly. Verify the product detail includes the category summary pointing to the subcategory rather than flattening it incorrectly, along with the seller summary, images, and variants. Confirm the endpoint returns the live product record for a product with multiple images and variants so the UI can render product detail and browsing context consistently for oversight workflows.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because the endpoint requires administrator access.

functions.name: test_api_product_administrator_retrieve_with_subcategory

scenario.draft: Test the business-facing not-found behavior when an administrator requests a product that is no longer available because it was deleted or otherwise removed from live browsing. Confirm the service does not return stale live product data and instead responds consistently with the platform’s unavailable/not-found handling for deleted or inaccessible products. This scenario ensures the endpoint respects visibility rules for removed products while still being an administrator-only read operation.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because the endpoint requires administrator access.

functions.name: test_api_product_administrator_retrieve_deleted_product

scenario.draft: Test that an approved seller can create a new sellable product with the required business fields: name, description, category, and base price. The scenario should verify that the created product is immediately returned in the response and is suitable for downstream seller management use. Confirm that the product is owned by the authenticated seller and is associated with the selected existing category, including support for choosing a subcategory as the product's category target. Also verify that product creation does not create snapshots at creation time, because snapshots are reserved for later edit workflows. This scenario should be executed with a seller account that is already approved to sell and with an existing category available for assignment.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller who is approved to sell, because product creation is restricted to sellers with selling permission.

functions.name: test_api_product_create_by_approved_seller

scenario.draft: Test that product creation is rejected for a seller who is authenticated but not permitted to sell, such as a pending, rejected, suspended, or banned seller account. The key business expectation is that the platform must not create any partial product record when the seller lacks the right to sell. Validate that the seller status gate is enforced before product persistence, and that the result preserves catalog integrity by preventing the product from appearing in seller product management or customer browsing. This scenario should use a seller account whose approval state makes product creation ineligible, while still exercising the same create endpoint and request shape as the success path.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller account that exists but is not allowed to create products, so the authorization and business-status gate can be exercised.

functions.name: test_api_product_create_for_ineligible_seller_blocked

scenario.draft: Test that a seller can create a product assigned to a valid subcategory and that the category relationship is preserved correctly in the created product. This scenario should focus on the marketplace taxonomy rule that products may be linked to an existing category or allowed subcategory, and that the created product inherits the seller ownership while remaining browsable through category-based product listings. Validate that the response includes the persisted category association and that the product is immediately available for later variant, image, and inventory setup. This scenario is important because category assignment drives browsing and search placement, and misclassification would break discovery flows.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an approved seller, because only authorized sellers can create products.

functions.name: test_api_product_create_with_subcategory_assignment

scenario.draft: Authenticate as an approved seller, ensure the seller owns an existing product, and create or select an existing valid category or subcategory that the product can be reassigned to if the update includes category changes. Then update the seller-owned product’s editable fields such as name, description, categoryId, and basePrice. Verify the response reflects the updated live product, the seller ownership remains unchanged, and a product snapshot is created that preserves the prior state for audit, including the product’s previous fields and presentation context. Also verify the updated product remains attached to a valid category/subcategory and that non-editable ownership-related fields are not altered.

This scenario validates seller ownership enforcement and product lifecycle protections on the product update endpoint.

functions.name: test_api_product_update_rejects_non_owner_or_deleted_product

Also confirm the update does not alter seller ownership or attempt to change seller account linkage. Include validation that the snapshot captures the prior product state for later dispute review.

functions.name: test_api_product_update_with_snapshot_preservation

functions.name: test_api_product_update_with_category_reassignment

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because this endpoint requires administrator access.

functions.name: test_api_product_update_deleted_product_rejected

Confirm the endpoint only returns preserved option history for the correct product-snapshot relationship and does not mutate any data when the snapshot is missing or mismatched. Call the endpoint for that variant and confirm the response is a paginated history scoped only to the requested productVariantId, with records ordered by the requested sort or default newest-first behavior, and each row exposing the inventory record id, linked variant summary, signed quantity change, reason text, timestamps, and soft-delete state. Validate filtering behavior by querying with reason text, quantity direction, and a created-at range to ensure only matching movement records are returned while pagination metadata remains consistent. Also confirm that the endpoint remains read-only and does not alter stock or history state.

Request the first page with a small limit and a specific sort order, then request another page to ensure page boundaries do not overlap and that pagination metadata correctly reports current page, total records, and total pages. Confirm the returned list preserves the requested ordering across pages and that the same variant context is maintained for every inventory entry. This scenario focuses on operational review of long-running stock history rather than stock mutation.

Then exercise two negative cases in the same business flow: querying a variant that does not exist should return the platform's not-found handling, and querying a variant that belongs to another seller should be rejected with the platform's forbidden handling. The important validation is that the endpoint never leaks inventory history across variant boundaries and never returns a history list for a variant the caller cannot access. If the variant has no history yet, confirm that an empty paginated result is still a valid success case for the owned variant.

Create or select a variant with several inventory movements covering both positive restocks and negative adjustments, then request its inventory history with default paging. Verify the response is paginated, ordered by newest first by default, and each entry includes the inventory record identifier, signed quantity change, reason, timestamps, and the nested product variant summary. Confirm that the returned records all belong to the requested variant and that current stock can be explained from the returned movement trail. Also verify that the endpoint remains read-only and does not alter stock or create new records.

functions.name: test_api_inventory_record_variant_history_listing

Verify that each filter narrows the returned records correctly, that pagination metadata matches the filtered result set, and that the records remain limited to the specified variant. This scenario should prove that the endpoint supports operational review of stock changes without exposing unrelated variants or mutating the inventory trail.

functions.name: test_api_inventory_record_variant_history_filter_and_sort

First cover a newly created variant with no stock movement and verify the endpoint returns an empty paginated result with valid pagination metadata rather than an error. Then cover a missing or deleted variant reference and verify the service rejects the request using the platform’s standard not-found handling. If the environment supports an access-control fixture, also verify that a caller without access to the owning product/variant context receives forbidden rather than inventory data. These checks confirm the endpoint’s business behavior for empty history and missing-variant situations without focusing on input validation.

Validate that the returned variant summary matches the same product variant scope and that the endpoint does not recalculate stock or expose unrelated history entries. Also confirm the record is treated as read-only history data by checking that the fetched content reflects the persisted movement record, such as a restock or adjustment entry, rather than any current-stock aggregation.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller because the endpoint is seller-scoped and requires a valid seller session.

functions.name: test_api_customer_cart_reuse_existing_active_cart

Cover a shipment that has already reached a completed or unavailable state and verify that a seller cannot resubmit or reopen it by changing carrier, tracking, or status fields. Confirm the existing shipment data remains unchanged after the failed update attempt, including carrier information, tracking data, status, and timestamps. This scenario validates the business rule that completed shipments stay immutable for shipping workflow purposes.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller who owns the shipment under test.
Prepare a shipment that has already been completed or otherwise marked unavailable for shipping actions.

functions.name: test_api_shipment_completed_status_update_rejected

scenario.draft: Test that shipment updates enforce seller ownership and shipment consistency rules. Verify that a seller cannot update a shipment that belongs to a different seller or update a shipment using conflicting tracking information that violates seller-scope uniqueness. The test should confirm the system rejects the change without altering the original shipment, and that no partial update is applied when the request would affect an unauthorized shipment or duplicate existing tracking data within the seller scope. This scenario protects both access control and shipment identity integrity.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller so the request is made under a valid seller identity.
Prepare a shipment owned by another seller or another shipment already using the same tracking number within the seller scope.

functions.name: test_api_shipment_update_cross_seller_and_duplicate_tracking_rejected

scenario.draft: Test that a seller can delete one of their own shipments only when the shipment is eligible for removal. Start by authenticating as the seller owner, create or load a seller-owned shipment that contains only the seller's own order items and is still in a removable state, then delete that shipment. Verify the response confirms deletion, the shipment no longer appears in the seller's shipment details or shipment list, and the underlying order items remain intact in order history with their existing statuses and preserved snapshots unchanged. Also verify that deleting the shipment does not change inventory, cancellation or refund request state, or derived order status beyond removing the shipment association.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the seller who owns the shipment.
Create or prepare a seller-owned shipment that is eligible for deletion before exercising the delete endpoint.

functions.name: test_api_shipment_delete_own_removable_shipment

scenario.draft: Test that shipment deletion is blocked when the shipment is not removable because one or more linked order items have already progressed beyond the allowed removal point. Authenticate as the owning seller, prepare a shipment tied to order items that have advanced to a non-removable state, and attempt to delete it. Verify the request fails with a business error and that the shipment, the associated order items, and all order history remain unchanged. This scenario should confirm that shipment lifecycle rules are enforced before any destructive action occurs.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the seller who owns the shipment.
Prepare a seller-owned shipment whose linked order items are already beyond the removable state.

functions.name: test_api_shipment_delete_blocked_by_non_removable_items

scenario.draft: Test that a seller cannot delete a shipment they do not own. Authenticate as one seller, prepare or identify a shipment owned by a different seller, and attempt deletion using the non-owning account. Verify the API rejects the operation for insufficient permission and that the foreign shipment remains available and unchanged. This scenario should ensure shipment management is restricted to the responsible seller and that no partial deletion or order-item mutation occurs on authorization failure.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the seller who will attempt the unauthorized deletion.
Prepare a shipment owned by a different seller so the caller is not the responsible owner.

functions.name: test_api_shipment_delete_by_non_owner_rejected

scenario.draft: Test that an authenticated seller can retrieve the shipment item list for a shipment they own, and that the response is a paginated collection of shipment-item summaries scoped only to that shipment. Create a shipment containing one or more eligible order items, then call this endpoint with the shipmentId and verify the page metadata and returned items match the shipment contents. Confirm each returned row preserves the linked order-item context needed for shipment detail views, including the purchased product/variant identity and item status, and that items from other shipments are not included. Also verify search, sorting, page, and limit controls change only the shipment-scoped results and do not leak cross-shipment data.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller because this endpoint is seller-protected.
Create the shipment that will own the items being listed.

functions.name: test_api_shipment_items_list_by_seller_shipment

scenario.draft: Test that shipment-item listing remains restricted to the shipment scope and the authenticated seller’s shipment ownership. Prepare two shipments for the same seller, or two sellers with separate shipments, then request the items for one shipment and verify that only that shipment’s items are returned. Confirm that items belonging to another shipment are excluded even if they belong to the same order history or share similar product names. This scenario validates the one-seller-per-shipment rule as observed through the listing endpoint and ensures the caller cannot use the shipmentId to inspect unrelated shipment items.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller because shipment ownership is validated against the seller session.
Create the shipment whose items should be visible in the response.

functions.name: test_api_shipment_items_scope_restriction

scenario.draft: Authenticate as a seller, create a shipment, and then retrieve the items attached to that shipment. Verify that the response only includes order items that belong to the specified shipment and that each returned item keeps the correct shipment-scoped and purchase-time context needed for shipment detail and order-history views. Confirm that the endpoint does not expose items from other shipments or unrelated product data, and that the listed items remain suitable for seller workflow review and customer tracking use cases.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller because this endpoint is available only to the seller actor.
Create the shipment whose attached items will be retrieved and validated.

functions.name: test_api_shipment_items_preserved_context

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated customer can retrieve the item list for one shipment that belongs to their own order. The test should prepare an order with a shipment containing multiple items from the same seller, then call this endpoint with the shipment ID and confirm the response is a paginated list containing only items in that shipment. Validate that each returned item includes the preserved shipment context and purchased order-item context, and that the list is stable for shipment/order-history display rather than exposing mutable live product data. Also confirm the pagination fields are returned correctly for the requested page size.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new customer account and authenticate as the customer who owns the order and shipment being inspected.
Create or access the order and shipment setup needed so the customer has a shipment with multiple same-seller items to inspect.

functions.name: test_api_customer_shipment_items_list

scenario.draft: Verify shipment scoping and ownership enforcement when a customer requests shipment items. The test should use a shipment that exists but does not belong to the authenticated customer, and confirm the endpoint does not expose another customer's shipment items. It should also cover the case where the shipment ID does not exist, ensuring the service returns the expected not-found behavior instead of leaking any item data. The key validation is that shipment-item browsing remains restricted to the caller's own order history and cannot cross shipment or customer boundaries.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate the customer who will attempt the unauthorized shipment lookup.
Prepare a shipment owned by a different customer so access-control behavior can be verified against an existing record.

functions.name: test_api_customer_shipment_items_access_control

scenario.draft: Verify that shipment item browsing honors search, sorting, and pagination controls while staying inside the shipment scope. The test should target a shipment with several items whose order-item snapshot context makes them distinguishable, then request a filtered subset using search and an ordering expression. Confirm that the page metadata is consistent with the filtered result set and that no items from other shipments appear even when search terms would match them. This scenario should focus on business-facing list behavior and ensure customers can browse large shipments safely and predictably.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new customer account and authenticate as the customer who will browse the shipment items.
Prepare an order shipment with multiple items so filtering, sorting, and pagination can be exercised meaningfully.

functions.name: test_api_customer_shipment_items_filter_sort_page

scenario.draft: Test the standard seller fulfillment flow for attaching one or more eligible order items to an existing shipment. Create an approved seller account, prepare an order with multiple shippable items that all belong to the same seller, and create a shipment for that seller. Then add one eligible order item to the shipment and verify the response returns the updated shipment composition with the attached item(s), seller context, and tracking-related shipment data. Also validate that the newly attached item is reflected as part of the shipment grouping and that the operation does not create duplicate shipment-item links when the same request is repeated in a way the business rules would reject. This scenario should confirm the endpoint supports bundling eligible items into one seller shipment and keeps the shipment internally consistent.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate the seller who owns the shipment and the order items.
Create the shipment that will receive the eligible order item(s).

functions.name: test_api_shipment_attach_eligible_items

scenario.draft: Test that the shipment-item assignment rejects a cross-seller mix. Set up an authenticated seller and an existing shipment owned by that seller, then prepare order items where at least one selected item belongs to a different seller. Submit the attachment request with the mixed item set and verify the shipment is not partially updated: no shipment-item links should be created, and the request should fail because shipments must contain only items from one seller. The test should also confirm that the original shipment remains unchanged after the rejected operation, preserving shipment integrity.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate the seller who owns the target shipment.
Create the shipment that will be used as the target of the mixed-seller attachment attempt.

functions.name: test_api_shipment_reject_cross_seller_items

Create an authenticated seller, an existing shipment, and at least one order item that is already attached to another active shipment but is otherwise eligible for shipping. Attempt to attach that already-assigned item to the new shipment and verify the request is rejected without any partial attachment. Confirm the shipment keeps its previous contents unchanged and the item remains assigned only to its original shipment. This scenario should also cover the immutability expectation that a shipment cannot accept the same item twice through separate attachment attempts.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate the seller who owns the shipment and the already-assigned order item.
Create the target shipment that will receive the item assignment attempt.

functions.name: test_api_shipment_reject_already_assigned_item

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated seller can retrieve the full detail of a shipment item that belongs to one of their own shipments. The test should create or select a seller-owned shipment containing at least one order item, then request the shipment-item detail using the matching shipmentId and shipmentItemId. Assert the response returns the shipment-item record with its own id, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt fields, plus the nested shipment summary and orderItem summary. Validate that the shipment summary reflects the correct seller, order, carrier/tracking fields, and lifecycle timestamps, and that the orderItem summary reflects the purchased quantity, status, parent order, product variant, seller, and timestamps. Also verify that the endpoint does not expose a shipment item outside the requested shipment scope. Include a negative check that when the shipment item is requested with a different shipmentId than the one it belongs to, the API returns not found rather than cross-linking data.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller who owns the shipment being inspected.

functions.name: test_api_shipment_item_detail_by_shipment_scope

scenario.draft: Verify shipment-item lookup is protected by the parent shipment scope and returns not found for detached or mismatched resources. Use a seller-authenticated context, then attempt to retrieve a shipment item with either a shipmentId that does not exist, or a shipmentId that exists but does not own the given shipmentItemId. The expected behavior is a not-found response in both cases, with no leakage of shipment, order item, or seller details. This scenario should confirm that the endpoint treats shipment as a mandatory parent filter and refuses cross-shipment access even when the shipment item identifier is otherwise valid.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller so the request is executed under the correct authorization actor.

functions.name: test_api_shipment_item_not_found_by_wrong_shipment

scenario.draft: Verify that a seller can retrieve shipment-item details only for active shipment records and that deleted or missing shipment parents are treated as not found. Prepare a seller-authenticated session and target a shipment item whose parent shipment has been soft-deleted or is otherwise unavailable. The endpoint should return not found rather than returning stale item data, because shipment items are subordinate to shipments and the parent scope must remain authoritative. Validate that no partial detail payload is returned when the parent shipment no longer exists in an active state.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller before attempting the shipment-scoped lookup.

functions.name: test_api_shipment_item_not_found_for_deleted_shipment

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated customer can retrieve a shipment item only when the shipment item belongs to the requested shipment. First prepare an order with shipments so that the customer has at least one shipment containing one or more order items. Then call this endpoint with a valid shipmentId and a shipmentItemId that belongs to that shipment. Assert the response returns the shipment-item record with its own id, created/updated timestamps, and the nested shipment and orderItem summaries. Validate that the nested shipment summary reflects the correct seller and order, and that the nested order item summary reflects the purchased item linked to the shipment. Also verify that the shipment item is scoped to the requested shipment and that no cross-shipment data is exposed. This scenario covers the primary success path for order history and shipment detail views.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because the endpoint is customer-only.
Prepare a shipped order with at least one shipment item owned by the authenticated customer so the target lookup has a valid parent-child pair.

functions.name: test_api_customer_shipment_item_retrieve_by_shipment

scenario.draft: Verify that the endpoint rejects a shipment-item lookup when the shipment item does not belong to the provided shipment. Prepare two shipments for the same authenticated customer, with at least one shipment item in each shipment. Then call this endpoint using a shipmentId from one shipment and a shipmentItemId from a different shipment. Assert the response is not found and that the mismatched item is not revealed through the wrong shipment context. This protects shipment boundaries and confirms the mandatory parent-filter behavior for shipment items.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because the endpoint is customer-only.
Prepare two distinct shipments for the same customer so a cross-shipment mismatch can be tested.

functions.name: test_api_customer_shipment_item_reject_cross_shipment_lookup

Prepare a customer shipment item, then exercise a lookup using a shipmentId or shipmentItemId that does not correspond to an active shipment-item relationship, such as a deleted shipment context, a detached item, or an identifier that belongs to another record. Assert the endpoint returns not found and does not leak whether the shipment, the item, or the association is missing. This scenario covers the key negative path for invalid shipment-item context without testing input validation.

functions.name: test_api_customer_shipment_item_not_found_for_missing_relationship

The test should prepare a shipment with at least one eligible order item, call the endpoint, and confirm the response returns the updated shipment-item relationship with the same shipment/order-item linkage model and preserved audit fields as expected. Also validate that the update does not break shipment grouping rules: the shipment remains seller-scoped, the item remains tied to the correct order context, and no cross-seller data is introduced. If the implementation supports a guarded no-op update for this empty DTO, confirm it succeeds as a safe refresh of the relationship rather than mutating unrelated fields.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller who owns the shipment and needs to manage fulfillment items.

functions.name: test_api_shipment_item_update_by_owner_seller

Set up two shipments under the same authenticated seller, create or obtain a shipment-item reference under the first shipment, then attempt to update that shipment-item using the second shipment's path scope. The expected business outcome is that the service rejects the request instead of reassigning the shipment item to the wrong shipment, preserving shipment ownership integrity. Confirm the response is a not-found or conflict-style failure consistent with an inconsistent path scope, and verify the original shipment-item relationship remains unchanged after the request.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the seller who owns both shipments used in the scope mismatch check.
Create the first seller-owned shipment that will supply the shipment-item reference for the mismatch test.
Create the second seller-owned shipment that will be used as the incorrect path scope for the update attempt.

functions.name: test_api_shipment_item_update_with_mismatched_shipment_scope

scenario.draft: Verify that the endpoint prevents a seller from updating a shipment-item assignment in a way that would violate seller boundaries or one-shipment-per-item rules. The scenario should involve a shipment owned by one seller and an order item that is already assigned to another shipment or belongs to a different seller's fulfillment context, then attempt the update through the current seller's authenticated session. The expected outcome is a business-rule rejection: the operation must not move the order item into a second shipment, must not combine items from different sellers, and must not alter shipment membership across seller ownership boundaries. Confirm that the service preserves the existing assignment and returns the appropriate conflict or forbidden-style failure for the invalid reassignment attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the seller attempting the invalid reassignment.
Create the seller-owned shipment that will be used as the update target.
Prepare another shipment or shipment-item context that already owns the order item so the reassignment attempt violates the one-shipment-per-item rule.

functions.name: test_api_shipment_item_update_reject_cross_seller_reassignment

scenario.draft: Test that a seller can remove one item from an editable shipment when the shipment contains multiple order items and remains valid after the removal. Set up a seller-authenticated context, create or identify a shipment that belongs to that seller and contains at least two eligible shipment items from the same seller. Delete one shipment item and verify the shipment still exists, the removed item is no longer associated with that shipment, the underlying order item itself is not deleted, and any shipment summary or item count reflects the change. Also verify customer-facing shipment details for the related order now show the item in the correct remaining shipment grouping and tracking information is still consistent.

Create or obtain a seller-owned shipment with multiple eligible items so one item can be removed while the shipment stays valid.

functions.name: test_api_shipment_item_removal_success

scenario.draft: Test that removal is blocked when the target shipment is no longer editable. Set up a seller-authenticated shipment that has already reached a locked state such as shipped or delivered. Attempt to remove one shipment item and verify the operation is rejected as a business-rule conflict, the shipment item association remains intact, and the order item continues to appear in the shipment details exactly as before. This scenario protects finalized shipments from being altered after fulfillment has progressed.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller because shipment management is seller-restricted.
Create or obtain a seller-owned shipment that is already in a non-editable state with at least one shipment item.

functions.name: test_api_shipment_item_removal_locked_shipment

Remove that only shipment item and verify the shipment's empty-state handling follows the platform rule consistently: confirm whether the shipment is removed or preserved according to the documented fulfillment lifecycle, and verify the related order item remains intact, is not reassigned across sellers, and that seller shipment grouping remains internally consistent after the removal.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller because shipment management is restricted to seller accounts.
Create the seller-side fulfillment record that will later contain the single shipment item used in this boundary test.

functions.name: test_api_shipment_item_removal_empty_shipment_boundary

scenario.draft: Test that an authenticated customer can create exactly one cancellation request for a purchased order item that is still in paid status and not yet shipped. Verify the request records the customer-provided reason, returns the newly created cancellation request, and initializes reviewer-related fields as empty/null while keeping the order item itself unchanged at creation time. Also confirm the request is tied to the specific order item, not the whole order, so other items in the same order remain unaffected. This scenario should validate the normal business flow for a valid cancellation request and the initial persisted state before seller review.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the customer who owns the purchased order item before creating the cancellation request.

functions.name: test_api_customer_order_item_cancellation_request_create

scenario.draft: Test that cancellation requests are rejected at the business level when the order item is no longer eligible for cancellation, such as when it has already been shipped, already cancelled, or otherwise moved beyond paid/unshipped status. Verify that no cancellation request is created and that the item remains in its current lifecycle state. This scenario should focus on the key eligibility boundary that cancellation is item-level and only allowed before shipment, ensuring the API does not create a request for an ineligible item.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the customer who owns the order item so the test can exercise the eligibility rule on a real customer-owned purchase.

functions.name: test_api_customer_order_item_cancellation_request_ineligible_item

scenario.draft: Test that the system prevents duplicate cancellation requests for the same order item. After one cancellation request has already been created for a specific paid, unshipped item, a second attempt for that same item should be rejected as a business-rule conflict rather than creating another request. Verify that the original cancellation request remains intact and that the duplicate attempt does not alter the order item or the existing request history. This scenario protects the one-request-per-item rule and the integrity of the cancellation workflow.

functions.name: test_api_customer_order_item_cancellation_request_duplicate_prevented

scenario.draft: Test that an authenticated customer can submit a cancellation request for their own paid, unshipped order item, and that the request is created with the submitted reason while remaining tied to that exact order item. Verify the response reflects the current cancellation request state, including the linked order item and customer-provided reason, and that the order item itself is not changed by this endpoint. Also verify item-level scope by ensuring the request affects only the targeted order item and not other items in the same order. This scenario should be run with a valid customer account and an existing eligible order item owned by that customer.

functions.name: test_api_cancellation_request_create_for_paid_unshipped_item

Verify that the updated reason is reflected in the returned request state, the request remains linked to the same order item, and no unrelated order item or order status changes occur. This scenario should also confirm that the latest customer submission is what seller review and dispute history will see after the update.

Confirm that the operation does not create a new active request, does not reopen a closed request, and does not alter the item's existing shipped or resolved state. Also verify that a valid in-scope request still works for an eligible paid order item, so the scenario covers both allowed and disallowed business states for item-level cancellation.

functions.name: test_api_cancellation_request_blocked_after_shipping_or_resolution

scenario.draft: Test the seller-authenticated flow for submitting a cancellation request against a single purchased order item that is still eligible for cancellation. Verify that an authenticated seller can create the request when no prior cancellation request exists, and that the response reflects the current cancellation request state tied only to that order item. Confirm the request stores the submitted reason, does not alter the order item status itself, and does not affect other items in the same order. Also verify the same endpoint can be used to update an existing cancellation request for the same order item, replacing the reason while preserving the one-to-one association with that item. Finally, validate the business rejection path for an ineligible item such as one that is already shipped or otherwise not in paid status: the request must be denied without changing the order item, order state, or unrelated cancellation data.
